  • -o json for scripts on the commands that report or create — status, explain, history, create bundle (also with --dry-run), promote, rollback and release-hold print JSON or YAML with -o, with the API's state values. The commands that create a Bundle print its name, pipeline, namespace, type, version and the pipeline's UI url (KARDINAL_UI_URL, else the dashboard address), so kardinal create bundle my-app --image app:1.4 -o json | jq -r .bundle names the new Bundle. Warnings go to stderr, so stdout stays valid JSON; -w prints one JSON document per refresh, or YAML documents separated by ---; JSON never carries the table's placeholders (history gives durationSeconds and running). The fields of each are in the CLI reference
  • The stage drawer in the UI — opening an environment (a fleet board station, a graph node or a lane) opens a drawer that says first why it is waiting: the pipeline is paused, a rollback holds it, a gate blocks it (with the gate's message, how long ago it was evaluated and the action that clears it), an approval needs N more approvals, a PR waits for its merge, the promotion failed, or an upstream environment is not live yet. Its actions each ask for confirmation first: Approve or Decline an approval gate, Override gate, Promote, Roll back to a chosen version (optionally holding it there), Release hold, and, for the whole pipeline, Pause or Resume and Reject version. Raw CEL and conditions are behind Details. The URL keeps node=<environment>, so Back and reload reopen it. At 1280 px and wider it is a column beside the page; narrower, a sheet. The UI API's gates carry gateTemplate (the gate's name as written) and maxOverrideMinutes (the controller's override cap), and its Bundles version

  • Approvals inbox, actions by role, change highlight and keyboard actions in the UI — Approvals in the top bar counts the approvals waiting on you and opens #/approvals: each approval gate still collecting its quorum, the longest wait first, with Approve and Decline (the environment's dialog), and below them the ones waiting on someone else and why. The UI asks the new POST /api/v1/ui/access which actions you may take: it answers only for the UI's own actions and valid names, with a SubjectAccessReview per distinct check in TokenReview mode (cached for 30 seconds, at most 300 a minute per user; a no is an answer, not a 403), and without TokenReview it refuses approving, which needs your identity; one you may not take stays in place but does nothing and names the chart role that grants it. A card whose state, version or approvals change on a poll gets a brief halo (an outline with reduced motion). j/k move to the next or previous environment (or approval), a approves, s ships a version; ? lists them. The environment details now also show the step timing bars, the running time, the step's events and, under a gate's Details, the controller's CEL check, as the node details panel did (Installation, REST API)

  • kardinal ship, with --wait for CI — kardinal ship my-app --image app:1.5.0 creates the same Bundle as create bundle (which stays). --wait follows it, printing each environment's new state on stderr, and exits with a stable code: 0 live everywhere it goes, 1 failed (or unreadable three times in a row), 3 held where a person is needed (an approval gate, a hold, a paused pipeline, a gate that does not pass and does not open by itself, such as one on a Bundle label), 4 waiting for a person to merge its PR, 5 replaced, rejected or deleted, 6 --timeout (default 30m) or interrupted (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM: the result is printed first). It waits through gates that open by themselves, those whose expression reads, outside its string literals, a variable that changes with time (schedule, upstream, bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes, metrics, changewindow; the list), and PRs the SCM merges by itself (pr.merge.auto); --stop-at-gate stops at any gate instead. Its last line names the version and its Bundle (Version 1.5.0 (my-app-x7k2p) stopped: …). -o json prints {bundle, version, url, result, exitCode, message, environments}. See ship

  • kardinal why, hold and unhold, and approve <pipeline> <env> — why my-app prod says in a sentence what prod waits for (paused, held, an approval and its count, "your approval" only when you may give it and otherwise who may (and, for an excludeAuthor gate on a version with no verified creator or one a kardinal component created, that nobody can approve it, and why), a gate with its rule, last evaluation and when it opens, its PR, a failure, an upstream environment, or nothing), then the version and the command that moves it on (Next kardinal approve my-app prod); -o wide is explain's table, which prints the command that gets past a blocking gate on stderr. hold my-app prod --reason … keeps prod on what runs there now, with no rollback, until unhold (release-hold) or --expires-in. approve my-app prod approves the version waiting for prod's approval gate, after saying which one and asking on a terminal (--yes answers); --version 1.5.0 approves only if that is the version waiting. approve <bundle> --env prod approves by Bundle name. hold again with the same reason is a no-op
  • Destructive commands ask first on a terminal — delete bundle, reject, override and a rollback of the last environment of a pipeline ask for confirmation when a person runs them at a terminal; --yes answers for them. Without a terminal (scripts, CI) they act without asking
  • kardinal init writes the smallest Pipeline, from flags — kardinal init --name my-app --repo https://github.com/myorg/gitops asks nothing and writes examples/minimal/pipeline.yaml: every default (branch main, kustomize, approval: auto, the default health check) is left out. --envs, --branch, --strategy, --prod-approval and --secret set the rest; without --repo the wizard asks only for what no flag gives. When a cluster can be reached, init finds the Argo CD Application or Flux Kustomization <name>-<env> of each environment and sets its health type. --create-secret creates the git Secret from $GITHUB_TOKEN (else gh auth token), labelled so the Pipeline may use it; --apply applies the Pipeline. The Pipeline is validated before anything is written; names must be DNS-1123 labels, --repo an https or ssh git URL and --branch a git branch name, and every value is written as a quoted-when-needed YAML scalar and checked by decoding the YAML back, so no value can add a field. -n default is written when given. --create-secret with an ssh --repo is refused with the command that creates an ssh-key Secret. Running it again with the same answers is unchanged and exits 0; an existing file or Pipeline with other content is replaced only with --force
  • kardinal quickstart: a demo on a local cluster in one command — kardinal quickstart --repo https://github.com/<you>/kardinal-demo installs kro, Argo CD and kardinal on a kind, k3d, minikube, Docker Desktop or Rancher Desktop cluster. In default it creates the git Secret (from $GITHUB_TOKEN, else gh auth token), an ApplicationSet for your fork, an approval gate on prod that only you may pass, and the Pipeline demo. It then ships a first version and follows it until prod waits for kardinal approve demo prod. It refuses any context whose name or API server is not local, whose cluster has a proxy-url or whose API server HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY applies to (the fix-it gives the NO_PROXY to export), or while HELM_KUBE* or KUBERNETES_MASTER is set, before it writes anything; helm and kubectl run on a kubeconfig with only that context (removed on exit, also on Ctrl-C) and with KUBERC=off. The Argo CD it installs polls git every 10s, so the demo does not wait 2 to 3 minutes for each environment to sync. A re-run changes nothing (Quickstart)

  • The stage drawer shows the command that approves — an environment waiting for an approval shows kardinal approve <pipeline> <env> (with -n outside default) and a copy button: the way to approve when the UI does not authenticate you

  • One way to say it across the UI — a version reads as its tag everywhere (the version rail, the header, the Versions tab, the sidebar), as on the map and in the stage drawer, with the Bundle name as quiet secondary text. The Activity tab names gates as the map does (the gate template), says "Waiting for approval" for an approval collecting its quorum, and shows the stage drawer's kardinal approve <pipeline> <env>. The top bar keeps the full width when the stage drawer opens; the drawer starts below it. A failed stage's drawer reads "Why it failed", with the failure message above Roll back. The comparison marks changed fields with a neutral marker instead of the hold colour, and a long CI run link fits its column. Labels inside UI-built sentences read lowercase, as status.summary does (one shared rule, web/src/sentence.ts)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• A git Secret is used only when it is labelled (#1506) — a Pipeline whose spec.git.secretRef names a Secret without kardinal.io/referenceable: "true" is Ready=False with reason SecretNotReferenceable and the command that labels it (kubectl label secret <name> -n <ns> kardinal.io/referenceable=true); kardinal status prints it as an ERROR line and the UI as an error under the Pipeline's header. Its git steps wait, before any git call, with the same command in their message and the GitCredentialMissing condition (reason SecretNotReferenceable); a render waits before its Job mounts the Secret. Labelling the Secret lets them continue. With scm.allowedRepositories, an unlabelled Secret that would let the repository through once labelled makes the steps wait for its label too, not fail with RepositoryNotAllowed. Same rule as every other Secret a custom resource names (Security)
  • -A that may not list every namespace fails — kardinal status -A and kardinal inbox -A refuse with "run … -n " when you may not list Pipelines in every namespace; without -A, status still shows the kubeconfig's namespace with a note. The controller line says needs list on deployments when it may not read the controller Deployment
  • kardinal reject and kardinal delete bundle take --name <bundle> — the Bundle of that name, never a version. When a name is also another Bundle's version, the refusal says --name is how to mean the Bundle of that name; and when they cannot check (they may get but not list Bundles), they refuse instead of acting on the name
  • kardinal why and kardinal inbox say who may approve from the server's own tally — both read the approval count, the rejecters and whether your approval would count from lifecycle.ApprovalStandingOf, as the PolicyGate reconciler decides. After your approval counts, why says approval by someone else (you approved) and inbox names "someone else who may approve"; a rejected gate says who rejected it (all of them) and offers shipping a fixed version or an override; a gate with more than 100 Approvals says to delete the stale ones. When inbox cannot read the version it says so, instead of "no verified creator"
  • kardinal get subscriptions LAST-VERSION is one token for every Subscription — a git Subscription's commit (abc1234, not config abc1234) and a helm Subscription's chart version (6.15.0, not podinfo 6.15.0), so the columns after it stay where scripts read them; -o wide shows the whole version
  • The CLI teaches ship, why and unhold — kardinal --help starts with quickstart, init --name … --repo …, ship … --wait and why <pipeline> <env>. unhold is the name of the command that releases a hold, whether kardinal hold or rollback --hold made it; release-hold stays as its alias. Help, prompts and explain say "version" where they meant one (rollback, reject, promote, history, diff), and explain says "held on rollback" only for a rollback. -o's help lists the commands that take json, yaml and wide from the commands themselves. get subscriptions has LAST-VERSION where it had LAST-BUNDLE: the tag, one word, so the columns after it keep their place (-o wide adds LAST-BUNDLE with the name), and diff's header names both versions (A: 1.28.0 (app-a))
  • kardinal status alone lists the pipelines — besides the controller line (now with how many of its replicas are ready) and the counts (Versions: where it said Bundles:), it prints one line per pipeline with its summary sentence, and how to see one; -n lists one namespace, and when you may not list every namespace it shows the kubeconfig's with a note. A caller who may not read the controller Deployment is told so. For scripts that read the text: Bundles: is now Versions:, and active is now in flight. -o json keeps its keys and adds controllerReady, controllerHealth, namespace, note and items
  • A gate's reason is a sentence that ends with the version — a gate instance's status.reason, which the CLI's REASON column, the UI, PR evidence and notifications show, reads waiting for approvals: 0 of 1 (version 1.5.0), !schedule.isWeekend = false (version 1.5.0), or with the gate's message Production deployments are blocked on weekends (!schedule.isWeekend = false; version 1.5.0). Evaluation and context errors and overrides keep their prefixes (CEL evaluation error: …, context error: …, OVERRIDDEN by …). The version is also in the new status.bundleVersion, for scripts (Policy gates)
  • Tables name versions, not Bundles — get pipelines, get bundles, explain, history and get auditevents have a VERSION column where they had BUNDLE, showing the tag and then the Bundle (1.5.0 (my-app-x7k2p); the name alone when there is no tag), and status and explain's deployed: line put the tag first the same way. -o json and yaml keep their keys (bundle)
  • kardinal dashboard port-forwards to the controller — without --address (or KARDINAL_UI_URL) it forwards 127.0.0.1:8082 (another free port when 8082 is taken) to a ready controller Pod's ui port in --controller-namespace (default kardinal-system), opens the UI and keeps forwarding until Ctrl-C, and prints http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ui/, the address it binds; --no-open only prints the URL. With --address it opens that URL. It needs create on pods/portforward there
  • CLI messages name the version, not the Bundle — ship --wait ends with Version 1.5.0 (my-app-x7k2p) stopped: … (the tag, then the Bundle), approve prints Version: 1.5.0 (my-app-x7k2p), and holds, prompts, explain and doctor say "version" where they said "Bundle" in a sentence. The lines that report an object by kind and name (Bundle my-app-x7k2p created …, deleted, rejected), which scripts parse, and the JSON keys are unchanged
  • A chart Bundle with a configRef is refused — POST /api/v1/bundles, kardinal create bundle and kubectl apply refuse a chart Bundle (type set or inferred) that carries a configRef: it promotes only its chart version, so the configRef would have no effect. Remove it, or create a separate config Bundle
  • The CLI's help is grouped, and every command has examples — kardinal --help lists the commands in five groups (Get started, Ship and observe, Approve and gate, Incident, Admin and debug) under a three-line getting-started block, and every command's help shows examples and a description of five lines or fewer. The full detail of each command stays on its reference page
  • One way to name a pipeline and an environment — promote, rollback, release-hold, override, history, logs, explain, metrics and policy simulate take <pipeline> [<env>] as arguments (kardinal rollback my-app prod); metrics, policy list, policy simulate and audit summary take the pipeline as an argument. Every flag form works: --env (-e everywhere), --stage (an alias of --env) and --pipeline. An argument and a flag that disagree are refused. release-hold is also unhold
  • More watch and all-namespace views — status and explain refresh with -w; get bundles, get steps and get auditevents list every namespace with -A, with a NAMESPACE column
  • CLI errors say how to fix them — when kardinal is not installed in the cluster, the API server cannot be reached, or the request is forbidden, the CLI names the context (and server), the user and the namespace, and the command that fixes it or the chart role that allows the action (viewer to read; promoter to ship, promote, roll back and pause; approver to approve and override). A kind the cluster does not serve while it serves Pipelines is reported as an outdated CRD, with the command that applies the chart's CRDs. A refusal by an admission policy shows the policy's message instead of a role, an unreachable server says why (connection refused, no such host, timeout) and shows its URL without any password, and override without --gate says when it cannot list the gates to suggest one. A pipeline that does not exist is reported with the pipelines the namespace has, also by get pipelines <name>, get steps, history and logs; an environment that does not exist lists the pipeline's environments, and so does a missing one. override without --gate lists the gates holding the pipeline back. kardinal init with its input ended says it needs a terminal
  • Durations in days — override --expires-in and rollback --hold-expires-in accept 2d, like audit summary --since; init --file has the shorthand -f
  • A 12-line minimal Pipeline, and a quickstart that sets only what it changes — examples/minimal/pipeline.yaml is the smallest Pipeline that promotes (git URL and Secret, three environments, prod approval: pr-review); the e2e suite validates it with kardinal validate -f and promotes a Bundle through it. examples/quickstart/pipeline.yaml drops the fields it set to their defaults (branch, layout, path, update.strategy, approval: auto), drops historyLimit: 20 (the quickstart uses the default history limit of 50), and says in a comment to replace the URL with your fork; its PolicyGates drop the kardinal.io/type: gate label, which nothing reads. The quickstart README labels the token Secret kardinal.io/referenceable=true
  • The version rail — the Map tab's versions are ticks on a time axis, newest on the right. Hovering one previews its route on the map; [ / ] follow an older or newer version, f the active one (marked Following), c compares the focused one. The comparison carries the map's marks (the followed version's red line, the compared one's ink dash) and lists each environment's state on both sides. Narrow maps get zoom buttons.
  • Table and Matrix views of a pipeline — the Map tab shows the pipeline as the station map, a Table (one sortable row per environment: state, what runs, what is on its way, gates, PR and actions; narrow screens open on it) or a Matrix (every version by environment, fleets and waves collapsed like the map; click follows a version, Shift-click compares). Links keep the view (?as=table, ?as=matrix).
  • The pipeline page is one station map (#1713) — the stage lane and the promotion graph are one map. Each environment shows the version it runs and, apart from it, the version on its way; gates sit on the edge into the environment they guard, an approval gate with its quorum, and the version you follow is one red line that stops at a gate holding it. Waves of five or more environments are one band and fleets one platform, each expanding to a grid with a row per state. The map opens at Detail, Map or Overview by the pipeline's size, and has search, a minimap, a list of what needs a person, and Promote, Roll back and Release hold under the environment in focus. Shift-click a second Bundle to compare its route. Gates, History and Metrics are tabs.
  • States read as words, the same in the CLI and the UI — one display table (pkg/display) gives every Pipeline, Bundle, step, sub-step and gate state a label, a glyph and a tone: a step WaitingForMerge reads "Waiting for PR merge", Verified "Live", AbortedByAlarm "Stopped by alarm", Superseded "Replaced by newer version", a gate Block "Blocking". The CLI's table output (get pipelines, bundles and steps, status, explain, logs) and the UI's chips and graph use the labels; -o json, -o yaml, the CRDs and the UI API objects keep the API values unchanged. The UI API serves the table at GET /api/v1/ui/display-states. A script that parsed the CLI's table for a raw state should read -o json instead.
  • CLI output fits where it goes — on a terminal every state shows its glyph and the UI's status colour, read from the design tokens: Live in spruce, Promoting in thread red, Waiting for PR merge in dusk blue, Held by gate in ochre, Failed on garnet (the only filled state). The exact token colours need COLORTERM=truecolor and a COLORFGBG that names the background; otherwise the nearest ANSI colours, which the terminal theme adapts. Piped output, NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb get plain words: no colour, no glyphs. The cluster's messages pass through as they are with a UTF-8 locale; without one, or with TERM=dumb, output is ASCII only (dashes and arrows fold to - and ->). kardinal status shows a REGION column when an environment has a region or a remote cluster, and -o wide adds ACTIVE STEP. On Windows colour needs a console with virtual-terminal processing. ERROR: and WARNING: notices are coloured too. doctor marks checks PASS, WARN or FAIL (✓ ! ✕ on a terminal), validate prints <file> is valid, and logs -f prints ->
  • kardinal status <pipeline> shows one row per environment — what runs there, a newer version on its way in, its state in words and since when, and its PR, after the Pipeline's summary sentence; then the gates holding a version back. Its columns are ENVIRONMENT, RUNNING, INCOMING, STATE, SINCE and PR; REGION, after ENVIRONMENT, appears for a multi-cluster pipeline (an environment with a region or a remote cluster), and -o wide adds ACTIVE STEP. It reads the Pipeline's status.environments and status.summary, the projection the UI shows, and computes them with the controller's code only for a controller that predates them. kardinal explain shows the steps, what is deployed, the gates and where the rest of a mixed image and config environment came from. kardinal get pipelines reads the same projection for its environment cells, so an environment shows its own state, not the cancelled step of a Rejected Bundle
  • A refused UI action names the role that grants it — the UI API's 403 for an action on a virtual subresource (pipelines/pause, pipelines/hold, bundles/reject, policygates/override) ends with the chart role that grants it, for example ; the chart's approver or admin role grants it (User roles). POST /api/v1/ui/override writes every instance it can when one fails, and its error names each instance that was overridden and each that was not, with why

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • The v0.10.0 deprecations — the API fields Pipeline spec.policyGates and spec.git.provider; environments[].shard, steps, promotionTemplate, regions and health.cluster; PolicyGate spec.selector; NotificationHook spec.webhook.authorizationHeader; PromotionStep spec.region; the chart values validatingAdmissionPolicy and rbac.integrationTestJobs; and kardinal rollback --emergency. kardinal validate reports a removed field as an unknown field with its path, as kubectl apply does. Each replacement is in Before you upgrade, items 7 to 10 (#1352)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The UI names versions in two more places — an environment held by a rollback said Held on search-rollback-3f9a1c by a rollback; it now names the version (Held on 4.0.3 by a rollback), with the Bundle name as the tooltip. The sidebar badge of a Pipeline held by gates, cut to Blocked by 2…, reads Blocked · 2 gates, with the whole state as its tooltip.
  • ship --wait gives each environment its own time — a held environment whose since is unset or zero printed for 2562047h47m16.854775807s; it is now unknown there, and the time this follow saw the state stands in. "took" is how long the environment's own promotion took (from its PromotionStep's first step, else from its upstream going live), not the time since the Bundle was created, and every time is clamped between the Bundle's creation and now
  • A version that starts a sentence keeps its case — status.summary (and so kardinal status and the UI) reads sha-9349a3f live in test, uat, not Sha-9349a3f live …
  • A soak gate says how far it soaked and when it opens — kardinal why, explain and status show soak 0.4 of 3 min in uat, opens in about 2m36s for a bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes or upstream.<env>.soakMinutes gate, from the Bundle's status.environments[].healthCheckedAt. For a gate that opens by itself, why's Next is to wait, and kardinal override comes only as Or
  • kardinal status shows an approval gate's tally — the Blocking gates table reads approval 0 of 1 for an approval gate, not its expression true (the column is then headed RULE). -o json has it in approval, and a soak gate's progress in progress; expression and message are unchanged
  • kardinal policy test takes -f, and a soak gate tested offline says so — policy test -f <file> works as kardinal validate -f does (the file as the argument still works). A gate that reads bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes no longer FAILs with load pipeline : pipelines.kardinal.io "" not found: offline its upstream soak is 0, and when that decides the result a Note says so and how kardinal policy simulate --soak-minutes evaluates it with a soak
  • kardinal quickstart refuses a fork that is not on GitHub — a --repo on another git host (Forgejo, GitLab, ...) was installed silently with scm.provider=github. quickstart now refuses it before installing anything and points to the installation and SCM provider guides, unless --set scm.provider says which host it is or kardinal is already installed
  • kardinal quickstart explains a chart that refuses its values — when helm refuses the values because the chart's schema is older than the CLI (a development CLI gets the newest published chart), quickstart says which chart this CLI needs and to pass --chart or --chart-version, instead of helm's raw schema error
  • Why a version failed shows where you look — a version that failed before any step (its Graph could not be built, kro rejected it, the spec is invalid) said why only on the Bundle (kubectl get bundle -o yaml): kardinal why said "nothing is waiting", status showed every environment live, and the UI showed no reason. The Pipeline now carries status.failedVersion (the Bundle, its version, the reason and message of its InvalidSpec or Failed condition, the environment whose step failed, and since when), cleared once a newer version exists; status.summary adds "<version> (<bundle>) failed before it started (<reason>)"; kardinal why leads with "The newest version … failed …: <what>", then its reason, the fix where known and kubectl get bundle … -o yaml; kardinal status <pipeline> prints it as an ERROR line and in -o json; the UI API serves failedVersion, the stage drawer's "Why it failed" shows it, and the Versions tab shows it under that version (Pipeline status)
  • A pr-review environment with an approval gate and a rule gate builds its Graph — every new version of such a Pipeline (the quickstart with prod switched to approval: pr-review and a gate of your own added) failed at once: kro rejected the Graph (compile node "GateMirror": ... found no matching overload for '_+_'), because the gate mirror added the two gate collections, which kro types as lists of different types. The mirror now maps each collection to the same entries first, then joins and sorts them
  • The UI names an overridden gate as you wrote it — after Override gate, the confirmation said the generated instance name the controller echoes (gate uat-soak--checkout-1-8-0-prod-us overridden in prod-us …); it now says the gate's own name (gate uat-soak overridden in prod-us …), as the dialog does.

  • One state per Pipeline in the UI — the page header, the sidebar badge, the fleet board and the health counters showed different states for one Pipeline ("Promoting", "Blocked by a gate", "0 Promoting"). They now read one state (paused, a failed version, held by a gate, named from status.environments as Held by gate prod-approval in prod, promoting, no version yet, up to date), as do the operations table's state column, sort and search; a paused Pipeline says Paused once in the sidebar and the operations table. Each Pipeline counts in exactly one of Healthy, Blocked, Failed, Promoting and the new Paused counter (one with no version yet, only in the total). The map's edge label names the gate that holds the version first, with its glyph (▮ uat-soak +1; in words in its popover), and a gate label never hides a station's, the breadcrumb names a followed version by its tag, and durations read 4d or 2h 15m instead of 96h 0m. status.summary no longer capitalises a version at its start (sha-9349a3f live in test, not Sha-9349a3f)

  • The map's toolbar on a narrow map — with the stage drawer open at 1280 (a map about 480 px wide) or on a phone, the attention items no longer wrap a word per line or sit under the search box: below a 720 px map they take a row of their own, each on one line with an ellipsis (the full text is its tooltip), and search, View and Zoom follow on the next row. The zoom buttons keep a visible Zoom label, and Fit the map is an icon, where it drew an empty box

  • ship --wait times never go negative — with the controller's clock ahead of this one, a summary's "for" is 0s, not -3s
  • A rejected version says rejected when the CLI cannot read it — kardinal why says who rejected it, and kardinal inbox leaves it out as it does every rejected gate, instead of "could not read the version" when the gate excludes the author
  • The stage drawer shows step timings, events and the CEL check — an environment's drawer shows the steps' timing bars and the running time in its evidence, the step's events in its history, and the controller's CEL check when a gate's Details opens (Installation)
  • No credentials from a URL in an error, a status or a log — a token in a URL (https://<token>@host/..., a password, or an access_token, token, private_token or password query parameter) could be quoted by an error: a URL that did not parse (a PromotionStep message, a RenderRun result), the git and Helm Subscription watchers' HTTP errors (the Subscription status, its Ready condition and the log; the git watcher sends a URL's credentials as basic auth, not in the request URL), and the HTTP errors of the SCM providers, MetricCheck providers and NotificationHooks. They all go through one helper (scm.RedactURL, scm.RedactText, scm.RedactErr), which also removes a password containing @ or whitespace and those query parameters, and the Subscription status applies it once more before it is written
  • The kardinal palette and fonts in the UI and the docs (#1698) — the UI and this site share one set of design tokens (web/tokens/tokens.json). Neutrals are spruce-tinted greys in equal light and dark themes. Cardinal red marks the followed release, the selection, links and focus. Status colours are distinct from it: failure is garnet, blocked is ochre, waiting is dusk blue, verified is spruce. Text is set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono, headings in Archivo. The fonts are served by the UI and the site themselves (SIL Open Font License), so neither loads a font CDN. The UI's theme button cycles System, Light and Dark: System follows the operating system, and a saved choice applies before the page draws. Every colour pair is checked against WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes
  • One set of UI controls — buttons, dialogs, chips, tabs and the drawer in the UI are shared components styled only by the design tokens, so they look and behave the same on every screen. Buttons are primary (ink-filled), secondary (a quiet outline), ghost or destructive (a garnet outline, for Roll back and Reject); none is red. Red marks only the followed release, the selection and focus, and links are ink with a red underline. Failure is a plum-wine garnet, far enough in hue from the cardinal red to tell apart at button size in both themes. A paused Pipeline's badge is a monochrome hatch. Sizes snap to the token scale, and Compact density tightens every screen
  • A link for every UI screen, ⌘K, and a pipeline page that leads with the map — every view has its own address: #/, #/p/<namespace>/<pipeline>, …/env/<environment> and …/v/<bundle>, plus tab=, compare=, view=ops, filter= and q=. A link opens it, a reload keeps it, Back and Forward walk it, and #pipeline=… links redirect to these addresses. A breadcrumb and a Go to or do… box (⌘K / Ctrl+K) are in a top bar; the palette lists pipelines, environments, versions and actions. A fleet station opens its environment, and a single Pipeline opens directly. The pipeline page's header has the name, Paused, Pause or Resume (the main action while paused) and Ship a version, then one line with the summary sentence and the shown version's commit, author and CI run; the tabs are Map, Versions, Activity (grouped failures and the version's gates) and Metrics. An address naming a Pipeline or version the cluster does not have says not found and links back
  • The UI says version, stage and gate, and says what went wrong — the UI names a Bundle a version, a PromotionStep a stage and a PolicyGate a gate; the Kubernetes kind and object name of an environment or gate are under Kubernetes details in its panel. States read as kardinal prints them (Replaced by newer version, not Sup; Waiting for PR merge, not WaitingForMerge), and a version is its name without the Pipeline prefix (Version abc123). The fleet board's badge for a failed version reads Failed. A Pipeline with no version yet offers Ship your first version. A failed read says what it means (the controller cannot be reached, a token was refused, the account lacks the viewer role, the controller is restarting) with the client's message under it and Retry. A ? button in the top bar opens help and the keyboard shortcuts. Under the Pipeline's header, a Pipeline that is not Ready shows an error (for GitCredentialMissing, which git Secret to create), or which git Secret to label kardinal.io/referenceable=true; it has its fix command to copy, as kardinal status <pipeline> prints them. An approval that excludeAuthor does not count says why as "the version's author (approval.excludeAuthor)"
  • One message for a cancelled stale promotion — a step the push guard (#1681) refuses because its Bundle was superseded or rejected says only why, bundle <name> was superseded — promotion cancelled (or bundle <name> was rejected), as a step the Bundle reconciler cancels does.
  • Release notes reach the GitHub release — the notes travel from the release workflow's preflight job to its release job as the release-notes artifact, which carries a changelog section of any size (a job output does not carry one of about 100 KB), the release job writes the body to a file the release step reads, and the release fails when the notes in the finished body are empty. The body's CRD apply command uses --force-conflicts, as the upgrade guides do

docs.title: v0.10.0 — 2026-10-11
docs.text:
The features teams moving from Kargo or GitOps Promoter look for first, 500-environment Pipelines and 200-Pipeline clusters, and every recorded identity verified against the Kubernetes user who made the request. Read Before you upgrade first: some changes refuse objects v0.9.0 accepted.

Requires Kubernetes 1.30 or later and kro v0.10.0-rc.0 or later with the GraphKind feature gate (hack/install-kro.sh installs it, now with 8 Graph workers and a 2Gi memory limit). The CLI is on the release page (kardinal-<os>-<arch>), and the chart now also publishes the kardinal-render image for rendered manifests.

docs.title: Highlights since v0.9.0
docs.text:
• Approvals, rejections and holds — approval gates with quorum, allowed users and groups and no self-approval, from the CLI and the UI; kardinal reject stops a Bundle everywhere; kardinal rollback --hold keeps an environment on its rollback until kardinal release-hold
  • Pull requests and verification — per-environment PR templates, labels, reviewers, assignees and SCM auto-merge; gate results as the kardinal/gates commit status; pre- and post-deploy hook Jobs; Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplates; Datadog, CloudWatch, New Relic and web MetricChecks with per-promotion queries; cosign and Sigstore image signature verification
  • Rendered manifests and fleets — layout: branch renders each environment in a sandboxed RenderRun Job and commits plain manifests to its branch, in both Graph shapes; a fleet environment expands to N targets with maxConcurrent pacing
  • Discovery, SCM and health — private registries and repositories, Helm charts, Kargo-style tag filters, pathGlob and push webhooks for Subscriptions; GitHub App and SSH git authentication, Bitbucket Data Center, and several SCM providers per controller (ScmProvider, ClusterScmProvider); remote-cluster health through a kubeconfig Secret
  • Scale — up to 500 environments per Pipeline (compact Graphs), controllers that reconcile in parallel and share their workers fairly between namespaces, Graph retirement for finished Bundles, many Pipelines on one branch, and namespace sharding. The scale suite's 9,000-Bundle soak passes every invariant with step p50/p99 of 1/3 s and a controller peak of 434 MiB
  • Security — verified identity for overrides, approvals, rejections, holds and Bundle creators, enforced by the chart's ValidatingAdmissionPolicies; only kardinal writes the objects a promotion Graph makes; scm.allowedRepositories; user roles with per-action authorization in the UI and Bundle API, Kubernetes tokens for CI; referenceable Secrets, an egress allowlist, an API access log, and AuditEvents that are never lost and retained within limits
  • Notifications and observability — Slack, Teams, CloudEvents and templated NotificationHook bodies with HMAC signing; OpenTelemetry tracing, SCM API and git metrics, DORA change failure rate and time to restore, and an OpenAPI description of the REST API

docs.title: From v0.9.0
docs.text:
Follow the tested steps in Upgrading from v0.9.0: label the Pipelines' git Secrets, apply the new CRDs (with kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts: the v0.9.0 chart installed them, so without it the apply stops on a conflict with Helm), re-run hack/install-kro.sh and helm upgrade --reset-then-reuse-values. Before that, check these changes for existing objects and clients (each is under Changed or Fixed below):

  1. A Bundle's spec is immutable. A script that kubectl applys a changed image or intent onto an existing Bundle must create a new Bundle instead (see Changed).
  2. Bundle artifact fields are validated. images[].tag follows the OCI tag grammar, images[].digest is an OCI digest, and the commit SHAs are hex. Check your CI first; stored Bundles keep working under CRD validation ratcheting (see Changed for the query that finds them).
  3. time is a reserved environment name. Rename such an environment before upgrading.
  4. New ValidatingAdmissionPolicies, always on: <release>-gate-overrides, -approvals, -bundle-rejection, -bundle-creator, -hold-writes, -graph-objects and the scoped-writes policy. Anything else that writes gate instances, PromotionSteps or PRStatuses, or a record in another user's name, is refused; another controller that legitimately writes them goes in admission.controllerUsernames.
  5. Label the git Secrets your Pipelines name: kubectl label secret <name> kardinal.io/referenceable=true. An unlabelled one still works in v0.10.0 (SecretReferenceable=False); v0.11 refuses it.
  6. Sizing: re-run hack/install-kro.sh (or set the same kro values: 8 Graph workers, QPS 300/burst 500, 2Gi limit). The controller's defaults are now a 256Mi request and a 1Gi limit; raise yours if you pinned the old 128Mi.
  7. Cluster-scoped objects: the chart creates a leader-election FlowSchema by default (leaderElectionFlowSchema.enabled); GitOps installs that cannot manage cluster resources set it to false.
  8. Graph retirement: a finished Bundle's Graph is deleted after 1 minute (superseded), 1 hour (verified) or 24 hours (failed), and with it its gate instances, PRStatuses, step detail and Events; AuditEvents and status.retiredSteps stay. graph.retire.*: 0s keeps the old behaviour.
  9. AuditEvent retention is on by default (90 days, per-Pipeline count limit); audit.retention.enabled: false turns it off.
  10. Deprecations: see Deprecated. Every deprecated field, value and flag still works in v0.10.0 and is removed in v0.11.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Compact Graphs render to branches — a layout: branch environment works in the compact Graph shape (more environments than --graph-compact-above, the kardinal.io/graph-shape: compact annotation, or a fleet): the RenderRuns collection creates its RenderRun once the step asks for the render, keeps it once kro created it for this Bundle, and the step reads it back through its own spec.live.renders; fleet targets render to their own branches, env/<fleet>-<target>, as pacing starts them; a fleet environment takes no render.branch, and a target's branch that another environment's render.branch names is refused (validation, and RenderedBranchConflict across Pipelines). Pipelines with more than 100 environments can use rendered manifests (#1515).

  • Fleets (environments[].fleet, #1457): one environment promotes a release to many targets (clusters, regions, tenants). The targets come from fleet.targets, or from a label selector over the targets' labels, over Argo CD Applications (each Application's path and health) or over cluster inventory ClusterProfiles. Each target is an environment of its own, <environment>-<target>, with its own PromotionStep, PR, PolicyGate instances and health check. maxConcurrent limits how many are in flight, and maxUnavailable failures stop the rollout while the targets in flight finish. Targets added or removed while a Bundle promotes join it or leave it (an open PR is closed). The environment after a fleet waits for every target. The Pipeline's status.fleets holds what a selector resolved to, and kardinal get pipelines and the UI's fleet board show a fleet as one column or station with its progress. A Pipeline with a fleet uses the compact Graph. See Fleets

  • User roles — the chart installs <fullname>-viewer, -promoter, -approver and -admin ClusterRoles (rbac.userRoles). Bind them per namespace with RoleBindings; aggregating them into Kubernetes' view, edit and admin is opt-in (rbac.userRoles.aggregateToDefaultRoles), since everyone bound to edit could then both promote and approve. The promoter and approver hold virtual subresources (pipelines/pause and pipelines/hold, policygates/override) instead of update: the UI checks them and makes the one change as the controller, recording the caller. rbac.userRoles.directWrites adds update for kardinal pause, kardinal rollback --hold / release-hold and kardinal override, and the <fullname>-scoped-writes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy then limits those callers to spec.paused, spec.holds (each with its subresource) or append-only spec.overrides in their own name, expiring within the override cap (controller.gateOverrideMaxMinutes), with the metadata unchanged. A test now holds 30 chained future-dated overrides to the cap (User roles)
  • Bundle API with Kubernetes tokens — bundleAPI.tokenReview (--bundle-api-tokenreview-auth) lets each CI system call POST /api/v1/bundles with its own ServiceAccount token, authorized by RBAC (create on bundles in the namespace) and recorded in kardinal.io/requested-by. The static token is documented as a single-tenant admin credential (CI integration)
  • Compact Graphs carry hooks, analysis and image verification — a Pipeline with a compact Graph (more than --graph-compact-above environments, or kardinal.io/graph-shape: compact) with hooks, verification or imageVerification was refused with GraphBuildFailed. The root steps and their pre hooks now wait for the Bundle's ImageVerification as in the nodes shape. A HookRun or AnalysisRun that kro cannot create is named by the Bundle's new RunsCreated condition. In both shapes, a pre hook no longer starts while its Pipeline is paused or its environment is held for another Bundle: its HookRun waits in Pending, without its timeout counting, and starts on resume or release. A pre hook of a superseded or rejected Bundle that has not created its Job ends Skipped, so an old migration does not run next to the new Bundle's. Post hooks are not held. Its HookRuns and AnalysisRuns now come from the HookRuns and AnalysisRuns collections, admitted on the same conditions as in the nodes shape (a pre hook with its step and after the previous one succeeded, a post hook and an analysis once the step is Verifying) and kept once they exist; the PromotionSteps collection reads their results back into spec.live, and an AnalysisRun nothing waits for gets spec.terminate
  • --pprof-address (chart value pprofAddress) serves Go pprof profiles (heap, goroutine, CPU) under /debug/pprof/ to diagnose the controller's memory. Off by default; a port alone binds to 127.0.0.1, so only a port-forward reaches it. See Memory profiles
  • Bitbucket Data Center / Server (--scm-provider bitbucket-datacenter, #1460) — PRs, comments, reviewers, approvals for bundle.pr.* gates, merge-commit detection, branch cleanup, auto-merge (pr.merge.auto: autoMerge on the merge call, 8.15+, while a merge check vetoes the merge; a PR with no veto is merged only with allowImmediate) and signed pr:merged webhooks. HTTP clone, browse and ssh URLs all name the repository, also in scm.allowedRepositories (host/KEY/slug, host/~user/slug for personal repositories) and in kardinal validate --allowed-repositories --scm-provider bitbucket-datacenter. Checked against the REST API 1.0 shapes only: the e2e suites cannot host Bitbucket Data Center. See Bitbucket Data Center
  • Compact Graphs mirror gates onto pr-review steps — the kardinal/gates commit status (#1518) is tested in both Graph shapes: in a compact Graph the GateMirror patch collection targets the steps of the PromotionSteps collection by name
  • PR controls per environment (environments[].pr, #1453) — templated PR title and body (the evidence sections are template functions, so a custom body keeps them), templated labels, reviewers, team reviewers and assignees ("{{ .Bundle.Author }}" assigns the Bundle's author), and merge.auto, which enables the SCM's auto-merge with a merge, squash or rebase method and a templated commit message, turns it off while the Pipeline is paused or a gate is closed, and never merges a PR with nothing pending unless merge.allowImmediate is set. Templates run sandboxed: no loops or variables, and every function is sized and counted before it runs, so a render is bounded by the template's length. A Bundle holds at most 100 images, and the image fields have a maximum length (repository 512, tag 128, digest 256 characters). GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea, Bitbucket Cloud (reviewers only) and Azure DevOps; the support matrix lists what each applies. A template that does not render sets the Pipeline Ready=False (ValidationFailed), and a control the provider lacks fails the step before the PR is opened. See Customising the PR
  • The hold-writes policy follows the release's scope — its binding matches the watched namespace in namespace mode and the shard's namespaces with controller.namespaceShard (the default shard also the unlabelled ones), like the identity policies, and it exempts the exact usernames in admission.controllerUsernames too, so one shard's policy never refuses another shard's controller (Sharding)
  • Subscription polls are traced — with tracing on, every Subscription request (OCI registry tags and manifests, token fetches, Helm repository index and OCI, git over HTTP) gets an HTTP <method> client span naming the host, under its subscription.Reconcile span and the egress guard; no trace headers are sent to the registry or git host
  • Private Subscription sources — spec.image.secretRef, spec.git.secretRef and spec.helm.secretRef read credentials from a Secret in the Subscription's namespace, which must be labelled kardinal.io/referenceable: "true" (otherwise the Subscription's Ready condition is False with reason SecretNotReferenceable and nothing is sent): a dockerconfigjson or username/password Secret for registries (the Bearer token flow of Docker Hub, GHCR, Harbor, Quay and distribution, Basic auth for ECR and Artifactory, identity tokens for ACR; ECR, GCR and ACR through token Secrets that a generator refreshes), a token for Git over HTTPS, and an SSH key with a required known_hosts for ssh:// and user@host:path repoURLs (#1454)
  • Helm chart Subscriptions — type: helm watches an HTTP chart repository's index.yaml or an OCI chart and creates chart Bundles (spec.chart). update.strategy: helm promotes them: helm-set-image writes the version at update.helm.chartVersionPath in update.helm.chartVersionFile (default Chart.yaml, the dependency named after the chart: .dependencies[name=<chart>].version); any other strategy fails the Bundle at build (#1454)
  • Tag filters — semverConstraint, excludeTagFilter, allowTags, ignoreTags, strategy (Auto, SemVer, Lexical, NewestBuild) and discoveryLimit on image and Helm Subscriptions; status.lastSeenTag (#1454)
  • pathGlob — a Git Subscription with spec.git.pathGlob creates Bundles only for commits that change matching files, reading back at most discoveryLimit commits; it was rejected before (#1454)
  • Subscription webhooks — POST /webhook/subscriptions/<namespace>/<name>/<provider> on the webhook port makes a Subscription poll at once, for Docker Hub, GHCR, Harbor, Quay, Artifactory and generic senders, authenticated per Subscription (spec.webhook.secretRef, a referenceable Secret), rate-limited per source IP and per Subscription, and idempotent; the kardinal.io/refresh annotation does the same by hand (#1455)
  • Subscription status — a Ready condition with the reason of a failure (SecretNotReferenceable, SecretNotFound, WatchFailed, ...), and observedPathGlob. Each poll is bounded (3 minutes for images, 2 for Git, 1 for Helm), SSH connections carry that deadline, and four Subscriptions poll at once
  • GitHub App authentication (#1460) — the controller's Secret (or --github-app-id, --github-app-installation-id, --github-app-private-key-file) can hold a GitHub App's ID, installation ID and private key instead of a PAT. Installation tokens are minted, cached and replaced 10 minutes before they expire; a key rotation in the Secret is picked up without a restart, as for a token; GitHub Enterprise Server works through --scm-api-url. A Pipeline's git Secret can hold the same keys for git. Chart: github.app.enabled. See GitHub App
  • SSH git (#1460) — spec.git.url can be an ssh URL with sshPrivateKey and knownHosts in the Pipeline's git Secret, for every provider; unknown host keys are refused. Every git connection, ssh or HTTPS, now fails after 5 minutes without data, so a stalled server cannot hold a worker. See SSH git authentication
  • AuditEvent retention, on by default (#1514) — AuditEvents have no owner, so they accumulate in etcd for ever, and a full etcd quota stops the whole cluster. With audit.retention.enabled: true (--audit-retention, the default; false keeps every record) the controller's leader deletes, every 10 minutes, records created more than audit.retention.maxAge ago (default 90 days) and, per Pipeline, all but the audit.retention.maxPerPipeline newest (default 1000). It lists them metadata-only in pages of 500, deletes at most 2000 a run, oldest first, and uses its own client limited to 5 requests a second. kardinal_auditevents_pruned_total counts the deletions. Records that name no Pipeline share one cap per namespace. The chart grants delete on AuditEvents only when retention is on. Upgrade note: after the upgrade the controller deletes the AuditEvents already past the limits (older than 90 days, or beyond each Pipeline's 1000 newest), at most 2000 a run. Export them first if you must keep them (SIEM integration), or upgrade with audit.retention.enabled: false and turn it on after the export. See Retention
  • Several SCM providers per controller (ScmProvider, ClusterScmProvider) — a Pipeline's spec.git.providerRef names a namespaced ScmProvider or a cluster-scoped ClusterScmProvider (type, API URL, token Secret, webhook Secret, allowedRepositories; a ClusterScmProvider also has allowedNamespaces). The provider is resolved when the Bundle's Graph is built and pinned by UID in each PromotionStep and PRStatus, so a step keeps the SCM it opened its PR on. A provider that is deleted or recreated fails the step instead of falling back. Each provider has its own webhook endpoint (/webhook/scm/namespaces/<ns>/<name>, /webhook/scm/cluster/<name>). Every use re-checks the provider's UID, its allowedRepositories and a ClusterScmProvider's allowedNamespaces, with namespace labels and Secrets cached for 30 seconds. The Secrets a provider names must be labeled kardinal.io/referenceable: "true". apiURL must be https:// unless scm.providersAllowInsecureHTTP is set, and provider API requests go through the egress guard. Each provider webhook endpoint is rate-limited. Pipelines without providerRef keep --scm-provider. The chart adds the two CRDs and read access to them. Run helm upgrade (or apply config/crd/bases) before you use them. See SCM Providers (#1459)
  • Roll back and hold (#1528) — kardinal rollback --hold --reason "..." [--hold-expires-in 24h] (and the Hold option of the UI rollback dialog) restores the environment and keeps it there until kardinal release-hold <pipeline> --env <env> (or Release hold in the UI), or until expiresAt. While it is held, no other Bundle promotes into the environment: their steps there wait, and one waiting for its PR merge is cancelled with its PR closed. The rollback is neither superseded nor garbage-collected. It passes the PolicyGates of the held environment that would block it only if the controller verifies it: its rollbackOf was Verified there, every artifact it deploys was deployed there by a Verified Bundle, and its artifacts are unchanged since the hold. Each pass has an EXEMPT: rollback ... holds ... (by ...: ...) reason, a GateEvaluated AuditEvent and a GateExempted Warning Event, and a refused exemption is named in the gate's reason. The hold is the new Pipeline field spec.holds. Changing it needs update on the virtual subresource pipelines/hold, which the new chart ValidatingAdmissionPolicy <release>-hold-writes enforces, along with createdBy equal to the caller. The controller writes HoldCreated and HoldReleased AuditEvents for every client. kardinal explain and the UI show the hold. New UI API endpoint: POST /api/v1/ui/release-hold. POST /api/v1/ui/rollback takes hold, holdReason and holdExpiresIn.
  • SCM API and git metrics — kardinal_scm_requests_total (by provider, repository owner, operation and result: ok, client and server errors, rate limited, network error, circuit open), kardinal_scm_request_duration_seconds, rate-limit remaining, limit and reset gauges read from the providers' response headers, kardinal_scm_circuit_state, and git clone and push counts, durations and bytes transferred over HTTP(S). An owner gets its own label only after a successful (2xx) call, at most 50 of them; the operation label has at most 100 values; values are cut to 64 bytes, the reserved ones are _other, _none and _quota, and repositories are never labels. Git endpoints with their own CA bundle, client certificate, InsecureSkipTLS or proxy use go-git's default transport and are not counted in the byte counter. The byte counter's service label is git_service: a label named service is overwritten by the ServiceMonitor's target label (exported_service), and a check now refuses metric labels named like scrape target labels. The Grafana dashboard gains an "SCM API and Git" row (Monitoring, #1529)
  • Controller sharding by namespace — controller.namespaceShard (--namespace-shard) splits the reconcilers across controller installations by the namespace label kardinal.io/shard; shard default takes unlabelled namespaces and the cluster-scoped kinds. A per-namespace token Lease kardinal-shard hands a relabelled namespace over only after the old shard's in-flight reconciles return, and a per-shard heartbeat Lease kardinal-shard-heartbeat-<shard> (one write per shard every 10s, whatever the namespace count) says whether the holder is alive: expiry is measured on the taking shard's clock, and a shard that cannot renew fences itself first. Tokens are only ever taken by compare-and-swap; the fence runs on its own ticker with every Lease call bounded to 5s, leaving at least 13s between the old owner stopping and a new one starting during an API partition. A second installation of one shard name refuses to take the first one's namespaces (ShardHomeConflict). The default shard warns (ShardNotRunning) about namespaces labelled for a shard nobody runs; each shard elects its own leader. kro is not sharded (ledger G13). See Sharding controllers (#1462)
  • Many Pipelines on one branch — git-push on an auto environment rebases its commit onto a branch another Pipeline (or environment) moved, replaying only the files it changed, and pushes again (up to 6 times, no wait in the reconcile); a commit that changed the same files re-runs from a fresh clone, and a step that still loses is retried with jittered backoff (at most 2 minutes, counted in status.contendedRetries, no limit) instead of failing. While a PR waits for its merge, a base branch that moved under the PR's paths, or was force-pushed, rebuilds the PR branch on the new head; a move at other paths only updates baseSHA, and a PR branch with someone else's commit is never rebuilt. PR branches are now kardinal/<namespace hash>/<bundle>/<env>, so equal Bundle names in two namespaces no longer share a branch (PRs already open keep their branch). PathConflict=True reports overlapping paths, including two environments of one Pipeline and a Helm valuesFile outside its environment, matches https and ssh URLs of one repository, and does not name Pipelines of other namespaces. Proved live with 10 Pipelines and 60 Bundles on one branch (#1461)
  • API access log — the UI API and the Bundle API log each login (TokenReview), each refusal (401/403/429/503, with the reason) and each write as a structured line (component=access) with the user, groups, method, path and status; never a token. controller.accessLog.allRequests logs every request, and controller.accessLog.sourceIP adds the client address, taken from X-Forwarded-For only for controller.accessLog.trustedProxies. Logins and writes are always logged; refusals and all-requests lines have 50 a second each, with dropped counts logged every 10 s and in kardinal_api_access_log_dropped_total (API access log)
  • Signed NotificationHook requests — spec.signing.secretRef names a Secret (labeled kardinal.io/referenceable=true, key signing-key, at least 32 bytes) whose key signs every request: X-Kardinal-Timestamp is the send time and X-Kardinal-Signature is sha256= + the HMAC-SHA256 of <timestamp>.<body>, so a receiver can refuse changed and replayed requests. A hook whose signing Secret is missing or unusable sends nothing. Verification snippets for Go, Python, Node.js and shell are in Signed requests
  • CloudEvents format — format: cloudevents sends the kardinal payload as the data of a CloudEvents 1.0 event in structured JSON mode (application/cloudevents+json), with the event key as id, io.kardinal.<event> as type and the Pipeline as source (CloudEvents)
  • UI fleet board — the start page draws every Pipeline as a line of stations: the version each environment runs and when it was Verified, environments promoted in parallel stacked, and a lit rail where the active Bundle is on its way (promoting, held by a gate, or failed). A station opens its Pipeline, and the logo returns to the board. GET /api/v1/ui/pipelines gains deployed (per environment: Bundle, version, verifiedAt, and the config or images it runs from another Bundle, as kardinal status shows them), activeBundleVersion and environmentTopology[].upstreams (What the UI shows)
  • UI Bundle type badges and keyboard access — the Bundle card names the Bundle type (image, config, image + config, chart), and the Bundle history tags the ones that are not image Bundles. A skip link is the first Tab stop; each fleet line and the Bundle history are one Tab stop moved through with the arrow keys. A light-theme, node-details and dialog accessibility check joins the WCAG 2.1 AA journey (What the UI shows)
  • UI step timings — a promotion's step list draws each step as a bar on the promotion's time span, next to its duration
  • update.strategy: yaml (#1448) — sets any YAML paths (spec.template.spec.containers[0].image, api.image.tag) in any files of the environment directory to a Bundle image's tag, digest, tag@digest or full reference, with image choosing among several Bundle images. Every edit is checked before any file is written, so a wrong path fails the step without a partial change. Symbolic links anywhere on the path, anchors, aliases and merge keys on the edited path, duplicate keys and a second YAML document are refused; an empty trailing document (--- at the end of a file) is accepted, also by the kustomize and helm strategies. See The yaml update strategy
  • Remote-cluster health through a kubeconfig Secret (#1458) — environments[].health.kubeconfigSecretRef: {name, key} names a Secret in the Pipeline's namespace; every health type then reads its object in that cluster. The Secret must be labelled kardinal.io/referenceable: "true". Only inline credentials (token, client certificate data, username and password) and an https server are accepted: an http server, exec, auth-provider, tokenFile, file paths, proxy-url and insecure-skip-tls-verify fail the step. The API server address goes through the egress guard. An unreachable cluster reports ClusterUnreachable: <class> (the full error goes to the log only) without counting a health failure, stops a running bake window, and is checked until health.timeout. The deprecated health.cluster string stays refused, with a message that points to the new field. See Remote Clusters
  • Rendered manifests: layout: branch (#1447, closes #1271) — an environment's path on spec.git.branch (a Kustomize overlay, or a Helm chart) is rendered at promotion time and committed as plain manifests, one file per object, to its rendered branch (render.branch, default env/<name>), which Argo CD or Flux syncs. The render never runs in the controller: each one is a RenderRun, a Job in the Pipeline's namespace from the new kardinal-render image (render.image), with the Pipeline's own git Secret, no Kubernetes credentials (a kardinal-render ServiceAccount without a token or role), a read-only root filesystem, no capabilities, memory, CPU and time limits (render.resources, render.timeout) and an optional egress NetworkPolicy (render.networkPolicy); its result comes back through the Pod's termination message. kustomize and Helm run in process in that Job (sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/api, helm.sh/helm/v4): a remote reference in any kustomization field, helmCharts, a symbolic link anywhere in the DRY source, an overlay diamond past 5,000 objects, an oversized template value and nondeterministic Helm functions (randAlphaNum, uuidv4, now, genCA, ...; allowed with render.allowNondeterministic) are refused. A rendered branch belongs to one Pipeline environment (the marker records it; a second Pipeline on the same branch fails, and gets Ready=False reason RenderedBranchConflict); any YAML or JSON file kardinal did not write is drift, and the marker is checked against the digests of earlier renders. A rollback renders only a full DRY commit on spec.git.branch from a render kardinal made. The render process has no network but git to the host of spec.git.url (Go's default HTTP transport refuses everything), and generator, transformer and validator configurations are checked for remote references too. A transient Pod failure (eviction) is retried, a permanent one is not, a Pod that cannot start says why, and a result is accepted only from the Job's own Pod, for the expected branch, and confirmed with git ls-remote. A render whose result was lost does not wedge the environment. image.digest and render.image.digest pin the images by digest. The rendered commit carries Kardinal-Dry-Commit, Kardinal-Dry-Path and Kardinal-Bundle trailers; a pr-review PR targets the rendered branch, so its diff is the rendered YAML; a change made to the rendered branch outside kardinal fails the next promotion (render.onDrift: fail, or overwrite); a rollback re-renders the DRY commit of the Bundle it restores. An ssh spec.git.url works as an https one: the render Job mounts the Secret's sshPrivateKey and knownHosts (only the keys its URL uses) and dials only the ssh host and port; an ssh session that does not use that dial is refused. See Rendered Manifests. Chart Bundles do not support layout: branch yet: they fail the Bundle at build. The compact Graph shape renders too (see below).
  • MetricCheck providers: Datadog, CloudWatch, New Relic and web (#1445, #1446) — provider: datadog (metrics query API), cloudwatch (GetMetricData, SigV4), newrelic (NRQL through NerdGraph) and web: an HTTP GET or POST to any JSON API whose value is selected with JSONPath and compared with the threshold, as a number or with the new threshold.text (eq, ne). threshold.operator adds ne. Every URL goes through the egress guard. See Metric Checks
  • Secret-backed MetricCheck credentials (MetricCheck half of #1267) — every provider reads its credentials from Secret keys in the MetricCheck's namespace (*SecretRef: {name, key}), including prometheus.authorizationSecretRef for an Authorization header; a spec never holds a token. The Secret must be labelled kardinal.io/referenceable: "true", otherwise the check fails with SecretNotReferenceable and nothing is sent (Secrets that kardinal may send). CloudWatch can use the controller's own AWS identity (IRSA, EKS Pod Identity) only with metricCheck.cloudWatch.ambientCredentials=true (--metriccheck-cloudwatch-ambient-credentials), off by default
  • Per-promotion metric analysis (#1445) — a MetricCheck with perPromotion: true is a template: each Bundle's Graph creates an instance for every environment whose gates read it, with {{ bundle.version }}, {{ environment.name }} and other placeholders replaced, once the upstream environments are Verified, and suspends it when the Bundle stops promoting (spec.suspend, also settable by hand). The gate of that Bundle reads its own instance as metrics.<name>. Values with characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._:@+-] are not substituted and the instance fails closed. The Graph identity's kardinal-graph-applier ClusterRole gains metricchecks
  • Only kardinal writes the objects a promotion Graph makes — the chart's new <release>-graph-objects ValidatingAdmissionPolicy lets only kro (the Graph ServiceAccount), the controller and admission.controllerUsernames create or change PromotionSteps, PRStatuses, HookRuns, RenderRuns, ImageVerifications and per-promotion MetricCheck instances, status included, and create Argo Rollouts AnalysisRuns labelled kardinal.io/bundle: a forged step, spec.live gate result, step state or merged PRStatus is refused. The Graph ServiceAccount counts only without a token or Pod credential (a minted token or a Pod running as it is refused); holders of the stock edit/admin roles, which can impersonate it, stay trusted as kro in their namespace (ledger G16; give tenants kardinal's roles plus view); HookRuns can be deleted only by kardinal, the garbage collector and the namespace controller; AnalysisRun protection is create-only. Deleting one still works (the Graph recreates it). The gate-overrides policy refuses turning an existing PolicyGate into a gate instance, so a PolicyGate made ahead of kro under an instance's name is never adopted with its pre-seeded fields (Verified identity)
  • OpenTelemetry tracing — tracing.enabled (--tracing-enabled, off by default) exports traces over OTLP/HTTP to tracing.endpoint, with tracing.samplingRatio (default 0.1, decided at each trace's root; an inbound traceparent is linked, not trusted, and does not force recording). Spans cover every reconcile, every promotion step, git clone and push, SCM API requests and NotificationHook deliveries, and inbound /webhook/scm and /api/v1/bundles requests. NotificationHook webhooks carry a W3C traceparent; an inbound traceparent on the public endpoints is linked, not trusted as the parent. Spans name hosts only, never URL paths or headers, and URLs in recorded errors are cut to scheme and host (Tracing)
  • Change failure rate and time to restore — Pipeline.status.deploymentMetrics gains the DORA stability pair for the last environment: deployments, failedDeployments, changeFailureRateMillis, meanTimeToRestoreMinutes and restoredFailures, over the last 30 deployments. A failure is a step that ends Failed, AbortedByAlarm or RollingBack after its change reached the environment, or a Bundle a later rollback rolled back from; time to restore runs from the failed deployment to the next Bundle Verified in every final environment (all of a fan-out's) and every region. No-op promotions, steps a supersession cancelled and rollback Bundles are not deployments (rollbacks count as restores; an automatic rollback's RollingBack step stays a failure), a deployed Bundle later rejected is a failure, and a Pipeline whose every deployment failed reports 100%. kardinal metrics prints change_failure_rate and time_to_restore, and the UI release metrics bar shows both (Change failure rate and time to restore)
  • NotificationHook formats — spec.format: slack posts a Slack incoming-webhook message with Block Kit blocks, teams a Microsoft Teams Workflows message with an Adaptive Card, and template a body you write as a Go text/template (spec.template), rendered by the same sandbox as custom PR templates (pkg/tmplsafe: no loops or recursion, every function call counted (2,000 per render), a 500 ms backstop per render, fields cut to 4 KiB, function arguments limited to strings, numbers and bools, 64 KiB rendered, JSON checked for JSON content types) with the PR templates' string functions plus json and truncate. An event the hook gives up on (a body that cannot be rendered for it, or 10 failed attempts) emits a Warning Event on the hook and counts in kardinal_notifications_dropped_total{hook_namespace,hook,reason}. json, the default, is unchanged (Formats)
  • NotificationHook credentials in a Secret — spec.webhook.secretRef names a Secret whose authorization key is the Authorization header and whose url key is the webhook URL (for Slack and Teams URLs that carry a token). The Secret must carry the label kardinal.io/referenceable: "true", the one opt-in for every Secret a custom resource references, so a hook author cannot send an arbitrary Secret of the namespace to a URL of their own; otherwise the hook is Ready=False SecretNotReferenceable (Secrets referenced by custom resources). The Secret is read on every delivery, so a rotated value applies at once. A missing Secret or key makes the hook Ready=False and events wait instead of failing (#1267)
  • More notification events — Bundle.Superseded, Bundle.RollbackStarted, Bundle.RolledBack, PolicyGate.Unblocked, PromotionStep.PROpened and PromotionStep.WaitingForApproval. Every request carries X-Kardinal-Event and X-Kardinal-Event-Key, and the delivery guarantees are documented: at least once, and no duplicate after a restart except for the one event in flight (Delivery guarantees)
  • Egress allowlist — egress.allowlist (--egress-allowlist) limits NotificationHook, MetricCheck and Subscription requests to listed host names, *. wildcards and CIDRs. Empty, the default, keeps today's behavior. The loopback, link-local and metadata deny list still applies on top (Outbound requests to user URLs, #1267)
  • OpenAPI description of the REST API — the controller serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document of the UI API, the Bundle API and the webhook health endpoint at GET /api/v1/openapi.json on both listeners (no credentials needed), also published as docs/reference/openapi.json. It is generated from the controller's request and response types, and a test fails when it drifts. The new REST API page lists the endpoints and shows how to give scripts their own ServiceAccount tokens (TokenRequest) with TokenReview auth
  • Pipelines with up to 500 environments (#1473) — the Pipeline CRD now accepts 500 environments instead of 100. A Pipeline with more than 100 environments gets a compact Graph: the promotion order is data in the Graph and one collection node creates every PromotionStep the order allows, so the Graph keeps about a dozen nodes. A 300-environment Pipeline (30 waves of 10, a gate on each) promotes end to end on kind in about 8 minutes, with a 0.47 MB Graph. The annotation kardinal.io/graph-shape: compact or nodes chooses the shape for a Pipeline, and --graph-compact-above (chart graph.compactAbove, default 100) moves the threshold. A compact Graph has no health ref nodes; health is still checked by each PromotionStep. See Large Pipelines
  • Compact Graphs carry per-promotion MetricChecks — a Pipeline with a compact Graph (more than 100 environments, or kardinal.io/graph-shape: compact) whose gates read a per-promotion MetricCheck (spec.perPromotion) was refused with GraphBuildFailed. Its instances now come from one MetricChecks collection: an environment's instances are created once its upstream environments are Verified, and suspended once the Bundle finishes, as in the node shape
  • Graph object limit — a Graph that would create more than 4,500 objects (kro tracks at most 5,000 per Graph) fails with GraphBuildFailed, like one over the size limit
  • Pre- and post-deploy hooks (#1443) — spec.environments[].hooks runs a batch/v1 Job once per Bundle and environment: pre hooks (migrations) before the promotion starts, post hooks (integration tests) after the health check passed. The new Verifying step state holds the environment until its post hooks succeeded; a failed pre hook fails the step before anything changes, a failed post hook applies onHealthFailure. Each run is a HookRun (new CRD, kubectl get hookruns) whose controller owns the Job: a finished hook never runs again, an edit does not touch a running hook, and deleting the Bundle deletes the Jobs and Pods. Hook Pods may run only as the ServiceAccounts in --hook-service-accounts (Helm hooks.serviceAccounts, default default) and must meet the Pod Security Standard --hook-pod-security-level (Helm hooks.podSecurityLevel, default baseline, checked with the upstream PodSecurity evaluator). The chart now grants the controller batch/jobs. Upgrading: apply the CRDs from the chart first (Upgrade): the release adds the HookRun CRD and the PromotionStep state Verifying. See Pre- and Post-Deploy Hooks
  • Analysis with Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplates (#1444) — spec.environments[].verification runs one AnalysisRun per named AnalysisTemplate or ClusterAnalysisTemplate after the health check, with the Bundle's tag, image, digest, commit, environment, bundle and pipeline as args; the environment stays Verifying until every run is Successful, and a Failed, Error or (by default) Inconclusive run, or the timeout, applies onHealthFailure. Every Argo Rollouts provider works. Without the Argo Rollouts CRDs, or with a missing template, the Bundle fails (GraphBuildFailed) instead of promoting unverified. See Analysis
  • Image signature verification (#1456) — spec.imageVerification verifies the Bundle's images before any environment is promoted: cosign key signatures and Sigstore keyless identities (issuer and subject), in Sigstore bundles attached as OCI referrers or in cosign's .sig tags, with sigstore-go, optionally from a separate signatureRepository and private registries. Selected images must be pinned by digest. commits.requireSigned also requires a config Bundle's commit to be signed with a signature the SCM verified (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea). Each Bundle gets an ImageVerification (new CRD); the first environments wait for it and fail when it fails. Secrets a policy names must be labelled kardinal.io/referenceable: "true". Bundles must be cosign image signatures (predicate https://sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1); a signature that does not verify is waited past until the timeout. subjectRegExp is anchored. commits.allowedSigners limits signers by login or email; commits the platform signed (GitHub web-flow, GitLab verified_system, the Forgejo/Gitea instance key) are refused unless web-flow, gitlab-system or forgejo-instance is listed; a signed commit must be a full SHA on the controller's SCM host. A policy change gives a new ImageVerification. The controller fetches the Sigstore public-good trusted root through TUF on first keyless use and refreshes it daily. update.strategy: argocd now writes an image pinned by digest as <tag>@<digest> (it wrote the tag alone). See Image Signature Verification
  • Compact Graphs carry approval gates — approval gates (#1510) in a compact Graph come from the ApprovalGates collection, read the Bundle's Approvals, and hold the environment until they are ready, as in the node shape; tested in both shapes
  • Reject a Bundle — kardinal reject <bundle> --reason <text> sets spec.rejected with your Kubernetes username (read with a SelfSubjectReview). The Bundle turns Rejected from any phase: no new step is created, steps that have not delivered the change are cancelled and their PRs closed (PromotionRejected AuditEvent), a merged one is still health-checked, and rollback, promote and Subscriptions skip any Bundle carrying its images (by digest when the rejected image has one, so a moving tag is not blocked) or config commit. Where the rejected change is live it stays the current Bundle in the views, marked Rejected with a roll-back hint, and the Pipeline is Degraded. The rejection is final, historyLimit keeps rejected Bundles, and the chart's new <release>-bundle-rejection ValidatingAdmissionPolicy admits it only in the requester's own name (Reject a Bundle, Verified identity, #1451). A rejection rejects only what the Bundle changed against the Bundle Verified before it where it went (status.rejectedArtifacts), so an unchanged sidecar does not block a rollback; with no predecessor, every artifact.
  • Verified override identity — kardinal override records createdBy as your Kubernetes username (SelfSubjectReview) instead of the local OS user, and the chart's new <release>-gate-overrides ValidatingAdmissionPolicy refuses an override in anyone else's name (the controller, writing for the UI, is exempt) and creating a gate instance, or changing anything in one but spec.overrides (spec and metadata), by anyone but kro, the controller and Kubernetes' garbage collector and namespace controller. The controller keeps one record per override (status.overrides: first seen, verified, audited; never dropped) and writes a GateOverridden AuditEvent once, stamped with the first-seen time. An override counts for at most --gate-override-max-minutes (Helm controller.gateOverrideMaxMinutes, 24h) from first seen; a future-dated one is not counted. createdBy is verified only while the policy and its binding exist (--override-identity-policy, which the chart sets); overrides already on a gate at the upgrade are shown and audited as unverified, and the UI API reports createdByVerified (Emergency Overrides, #1450, #1286)
