The UI API refuses a longer override, and the chart's scoped-writes admission policy one written with kubectl by a caller limited to policygates/override (Helm controller.gateOverrideMaxMinutes). --gate-status-heartbeat duration 10m0s Longest a PolicyGate's status goes unwritten while its result does not change. Each status write makes kro re-check the gate's whole Graph. 0 writes the status on every evaluation. --gates-commit-status bool true Post the gate results of a waiting pr-review step as a commit status on its PR (Helm scm.gatesCommitStatus.enabled). false posts none, for a token without the commit-status permission. --gates-status-context string "kardinal/gates" Commit status context (GitLab name, Bitbucket key, Azure DevOps genre/name) the gate results are posted under (Helm scm.gatesCommitStatus.context). Reserved for kardinal: branch protection requires it, so nothing else may post under it. --github-app-id int GitHub App ID: authenticate as a GitHub App installation instead of with --github-token. Needs --github-app-installation-id and --github-app-private-key-file. Also readable from GITHUB_APP_ID. --github-app-installation-id int GitHub App installation ID. Also readable from GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID. --github-app-private-key-file string File holding the GitHub App private key (PEM). Also readable from GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE. --github-token string SCM token for API operations (a GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps token). --graph-applier-clusterrole string "kardinal-graph-applier" ClusterRole bound to the Graph ServiceAccount in the Pipeline namespace. --graph-compact-above int 100 Environment count above which a Bundle's Graph uses the compact shape (one PromotionStep collection) when the Pipeline's kardinal.io/graph-shape annotation does not choose one. 0 makes every Graph compact. --graph-reader-clusterrole string "kardinal-graph-reader" ClusterRole bound to the Graph ServiceAccount in namespaces its health checks read. --graph-reader-namespaces string "argocd,flux-system" Comma-separated namespaces, besides a Graph's own namespace, where the Graph ServiceAccount may be bound to the reader ClusterRole for health checks. "*" allows every namespace except kube-system, kube-public and kube-node-lease. Health checks in other namespaces get no Graph ref. --graph-retire-failed-after duration 24h0m0s How long the Graph of a Failed Bundle is kept before it is retired. A retired Failed Bundle does not recover. 0 keeps it. --graph-retire-superseded-after duration 1m0s How long the Graph of a Superseded Bundle, or of a Verified one a newer Bundle replaced in every environment, is kept before it is retired (deleted; the Bundle keeps its PromotionSteps in status.retiredSteps). 0 keeps it. --graph-retire-verified-after duration 1h0m0s How long the Graph of a Verified Bundle that is still deployed in an environment is kept before it is retired. 0 keeps it. --graph-service-account string "kardinal-graph" ServiceAccount (created in each Pipeline namespace) that kro impersonates to apply Graphs. --health-probe-bind-address string ":8081" The address the probe endpoint binds to. --health-refresh bool true Ask Argo CD (argocd.argoproj.io/refresh) or Flux (reconcile.fluxcd.io/requestedAt) to sync a promotion's commit as soon as it is in git, once per step, instead of waiting for their poll (Helm health.refresh.enabled). An environment's health.refresh: false turns it off there. --hold-bundle-grace duration 2m0s How long a hold (Pipeline spec.holds) may name a rollback Bundle that does not exist before the controller reports it (condition HoldBundleMissing, a Warning Event, an AuditEvent). The hold stays in effect. --hook-pod-security-level string "baseline" Pod Security Standard a hook Job Pod must meet: baseline (default), restricted or privileged (no Pod checks). Below privileged, nodeName and hostPort are refused too. A hook that breaks it fails without running. See docs/hooks.md. --hook-service-accounts string "default" Comma-separated ServiceAccount names a Pipeline hook's Job Pod may run as (in the Pipeline namespace). A hook whose Pod names another ServiceAccount fails without running. The Graph ServiceAccount (--graph-service-account) is never allowed. See docs/hooks.md. --kubeconfig string Paths to a kubeconfig. Only required if out-of-cluster. --leader-elect bool false Enable leader election for controller manager. Enabling this will ensure there is only one active controller manager. --log-level string "info" Log level for zerolog. One of: debug, info, warn, error. --metriccheck-cloudwatch-ambient-credentials bool false Let cloudwatch MetricChecks without credential Secret refs use the controller's own AWS identity (SDK default chain: environment, IRSA, EKS Pod Identity). Off by default. --metriccheck-global-slots int 12 Most MetricCheck queries running at once in the cluster (at least 1). The rest wait, first come, first served. The MetricCheck controller runs this many workers plus 4, at least 16. --metriccheck-namespace-slots int 1 Most MetricCheck queries of one namespace running at once (at least 1). --metrics-bind-address string ":8080" The address the metric endpoint binds to. --namespace-shard string Shard this controller reconciles: namespaces labelled kardinal.io/shard=<name>; "default" also takes namespaces without the label and the cluster-scoped kinds. Empty (the default): no sharding, every namespace. Every controller of a sharded cluster needs a shard name. Also readable from KARDINAL_NAMESPACE_SHARD. --override-identity-policy string Name of the chart's gate-overrides ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and binding. The controller records an override's createdBy as verified only while both exist; empty records every override unverified. --pipeline-workers int 4 How many Pipelines (status, history) are reconciled at once. --policy-namespaces string "platform-policies" Comma-separated list of namespaces to scan for org-level PolicyGates. --policygate-workers int 8 How many PolicyGates (CEL evaluation) are reconciled at once. --pprof-address string Address that serves Go's net/http/pprof profiles (heap, goroutine, CPU) under /debug/pprof/, with no authentication. Only an empty value (the default) disables it; an address without a host, such as :6060, binds to 127.0.0.1 only. --promotionstep-workers int 16 How many PromotionSteps (git clone, commit, push, PR, health check) are reconciled at once. --prstatus-workers int 8 How many PRStatuses (SCM polls) are reconciled at once. --render-cpu-limit string "1" CPU limit of a render Job. --render-image string The kardinal-render image the render Jobs of layout: branch environments run. Empty: layout: branch promotions fail with a message naming this flag. --render-image-pull-policy string imagePullPolicy of the render Jobs (default: Kubernetes'). --render-image-pull-secrets string Comma-separated imagePullSecrets of the render Pods (Secrets in the Pipeline namespace). --render-memory-limit string "512Mi" Memory limit of a render Job; a render that needs more fails. --render-service-account string "kardinal-render" ServiceAccount the render Jobs run as, in the Pipeline namespace. The controller creates it there, without a token, when it is missing; bind no role to it. --render-timeout duration 5m0s How long a render Job may run (its activeDeadlineSeconds). --scm-allowed-repositories string Comma-separated host/repository globs (github.com/acme/, gitlab.example.com/team/*) of the repositories the controller's SCM token may act on. Every SCM call for another repository is refused, and a Pipeline that would need the token for one is Ready=False/RepositoryNotAllowed and its steps fail. Empty allows every repository. --scm-api-url string SCM API base URL override (e.g. for GitHub Enterprise or self-managed GitLab). --scm-instance-signers string Comma-separated names or emails the Forgejo/Gitea instance signs commits with (repository.signing SIGNING_NAME / SIGNING_EMAIL). Image verification treats a commit signed by one as a platform signature (forgejo-instance), refused unless commits.allowedSigners lists forgejo-instance. Without it, a verified signer that is not a user of the instance is the instance key. --scm-provider string SCM provider type for the whole controller: "github" (default), "gitlab", "forgejo", "gitea", "bitbucket", "azuredevops" or "bitbucket-datacenter" (needs --scm-api-url). --scm-providers-allow-http bool false Let ScmProviders and ClusterScmProviders use an http:// spec.apiURL, for an in-cluster SCM without TLS. Off, a provider must use https://, so its token never crosses the network in clear text. --scm-token-secret-key string Data key within the Secret that holds the SCM token (default: "token"). Also readable from KARDINAL_SCM_TOKEN_SECRET_KEY environment variable. --scm-token-secret-name string Name of a Kubernetes Secret whose data key contains the SCM token. When set, the controller watches this Secret and reloads the SCM provider on token change — no restart required (zero-downtime credential rotation). Also readable from KARDINAL_SCM_TOKEN_SECRET_NAME environment variable. --scm-token-secret-namespace string Namespace of the Secret named by --scm-token-secret-name. Defaults to the POD_NAMESPACE environment variable, then 'kardinal-system'. Also readable from KARDINAL_SCM_TOKEN_SECRET_NAMESPACE environment variable. --scm-wait-timeout duration 30m0s Longest a PromotionStep waits for an open SCM circuit (its SCM host keeps failing) before it fails, when its environment sets no stepTimeoutSeconds. --tls-cert-file string Path to the TLS certificate file (PEM). When set together with --tls-key-file, both the UI and webhook servers use HTTPS instead of plain HTTP. Also readable from KARDINAL_TLS_CERT_FILE environment variable. --tls-key-file string Path to the TLS private key file (PEM). When set together with --tls-cert-file, both the UI and webhook servers use HTTPS instead of plain HTTP. Also readable from KARDINAL_TLS_KEY_FILE environment variable. --tokenreview-accept-apiserver-audience bool false Also accept tokens for the API server's own audience (kubeconfig and default ServiceAccount tokens). Such a token also works against the API server, so kardinal could replay it; off by default. Chart value: tokenReview.acceptAPIServerAudience. --tokenreview-audiences string "kardinal-promoter" Comma-separated token audiences the UI API and the Bundle API accept in TokenReview mode. Mint tokens with kubectl create token <sa> --audience kardinal-promoter. Chart value: tokenReview.audiences. Also readable from KARDINAL_TOKENREVIEW_AUDIENCES. --tracing-enabled bool false Export OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP/HTTP: a span per reconcile, promotion step, git clone and push, SCM API request and NotificationHook delivery, and server spans for /webhook/scm and /api/v1/bundles. Off by default. Chart value: tracing.enabled. Also readable from KARDINAL_TRACING_ENABLED. --tracing-endpoint string OTLP/HTTP endpoint: a URL (http://otel-collector.observability:4318; /v1/traces is added) or host:port. Empty uses OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, else localhost:4318. Chart value: tracing.endpoint. --tracing-insecure bool false Send traces over plain HTTP to a host:port --tracing-endpoint. Chart value: tracing.insecure. --tracing-sampling-ratio float 0.1 Fraction of traces recorded, 0 to 1, decided once per trace at its root (a reconcile, or an inbound request: an inbound traceparent is linked, not trusted, so it does not force sampling). Chart value: tracing.samplingRatio. --ui-allowed-hosts string Comma-separated host names (no scheme; a port is ignored) the UI server answers to, on top of localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1: the controller Service DNS names and any Ingress host. A request counts as same-origin only when its Host header is one of these, and while UI auth is off, every /api/ request with any other Host is rejected with 403, reads included (DNS rebinding protection). Static /ui/ assets are not checked. Chart value: ui.allowedHosts. Also readable from KARDINAL_UI_ALLOWED_HOSTS environment variable. --ui-auth-static-overrides-tokenreview bool false Start even when both --ui-auth-token and --ui-tokenreview-auth are set; the static token then wins and every UI caller acts as the controller. Without it that combination stops the controller. Chart value: ui.auth.allowStaticTokenWithTokenReview. --ui-auth-token string Bearer token for authenticating /api/v1/ui/* requests. When set, all UI API routes require 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. When empty (default) and --ui-tokenreview-auth is off, /api/ answers only loopback clients (kubectl port-forward) and refuses the rest with 403. Also readable from KARDINAL_UI_TOKEN environment variable. --ui-listen-address string ":8082" The address the embedded kardinal-ui HTTP server binds to. --ui-tokenreview-auth bool false Enable Kubernetes TokenReview-based authentication for /api/v1/ui/* routes. When true and --ui-auth-token is not set, each request's bearer token is validated via authenticationv1.TokenReview. Fail-closed: API errors return 503. Also readable from KARDINAL_UI_TOKENREVIEW_AUTH environment variable (set to 'true'). --watch-namespace string Namespace to watch (default: "" = cluster-wide). When set, the controller only reconciles resources in the given namespace and expects a Role/RoleBinding instead of a ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding. Also readable from KARDINAL_WATCH_NAMESPACE environment variable. --webhook-bind-address string ":8083" The address the SCM webhook endpoint binds to. --webhook-secret string Secret for validating incoming SCM webhooks (an HMAC key or a shared token, depending on the provider; see docs/scm-providers.md). --zap-devel bool false Development Mode defaults(encoder=consoleEncoder,logLevel=Debug,stackTraceLevel=Warn). Production Mode defaults(encoder=jsonEncoder,logLevel=Info,stackTraceLevel=Error) --zap-encoder value Zap log encoding (one of 'json' or 'console') --zap-log-level value Zap Level to configure the verbosity of logging. Can be one of 'debug', 'info', 'error', 'panic' or any integer value > 0 which corresponds to custom debug levels of increasing verbosity --zap-stacktrace-level value Zap Level at and above which stacktraces are captured (one of 'info', 'error', 'panic'). --zap-time-encoding value Zap time encoding (one of 'epoch', 'millis', 'nano', 'iso8601', 'rfc3339' or 'rfc3339nano'). Defaults to 'epoch'.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
kardinal has four core words: version, pipeline, environment and gate (Concepts). Every other term maps to one of them or to an object they use.

Term Kubernetes kind or field Meaning Shown as Version Bundle A version of your app: one immutable snapshot of what to deploy (images, a chart version or a config commit) with its provenance. The kardinal create bundle and get bundles commands act on versions Pipeline Pipeline The promotion path of one application: its Git repository and its environments, in order Environment Pipeline spec.environments[] One place a version is deployed to, such as test, uat or prod; its directory or branch in the GitOps repository Stage, promotion step PromotionStep The promotion of one version into one environment: commit or pull request, merge, health check. kardinal creates them its state: Queued, Live, ... Gate PolicyGate A CEL expression that holds a version out of an environment until it is true its state: Passing, Blocking, ... Org gate, team gate PolicyGate in a --policy-namespaces namespace, or in the Pipeline's An org gate applies to every Pipeline and teams cannot remove it; a team gate adds to it Approval gate PolicyGate spec.approval, Approval A gate that passes once enough people ran kardinal approve Override PolicyGate spec.overrides[] A time-limited, recorded force-pass of a gate (kardinal override) Change window ChangeWindow A cluster-wide blackout or allowed-hours window a gate can read Metric check MetricCheck A metric query with a threshold a gate can read (metrics.<name>) Soak, bake upstream.<env>.soakMinutes, bake How long a version has been Verified in an upstream environment. upstream.<env>.soakMinutes names the environment; bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes is shorthand for the direct upstream (the minimum on fan-in). bake requires continuous health before Verified Health check health How a promotion step decides its environment runs the version healthily (Deployment, Argo CD, Flux, Argo Rollouts, Flagger) Hook hooks, HookRun A Job that runs before a promotion or after its health check Wave wave A number that promotes environments with the same number in parallel Fleet fleet One environment expanded to many targets, promoted with a pace Supersede phase Superseded A newer version of the same type replaces an unfinished older one (details) Replaced by newer version Reject spec.rejected Stop a version everywhere for good (kardinal reject) Rejected (a version), Version rejected (a gate) Hold Pipeline spec.holds Keep an environment on a rolled-back version (kardinal rollback --hold) Held by rollback Pause Pipeline spec.paused Stop new promotions of a Pipeline (kardinal pause) Paused PR evidence The provenance, gate results and upstream health kardinal writes into a promotion pull request Subscription Subscription Watches a registry, Git or a chart repository and creates versions Rendered manifests layout: branch, RenderRun kardinal renders an environment and commits plain YAML to its branch Graph kro Graph The DAG kardinal builds for each version; kro creates its gates and promotion steps (Architecture) Retire condition GraphRetired Delete a finished version's Graph, keeping a record of its steps (details) Audit event AuditEvent An immutable record of a promotion transition (Audit logging)

docs.title: States and how they are shown
docs.text: The CLI's tables and the UI show each state as a label; -o json, -o yaml, the Kubernetes objects and the UI API keep the API value. The UI API serves this table at GET /api/v1/ui/display-states.

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text: API value Shown as Unknown No version yet Promoting Promoting Ready Up to date Degraded A version failed Paused Paused

docs.title: Version
docs.text: API value Shown as Available Ready to promote Promoting Promoting Verified Verified Failed Failed Superseded Replaced by newer version Rejected Rejected

docs.title: Promotion step
docs.text:
API value Shown as NotStarted Not reached Pending Queued Promoting Promoting WaitingForMerge Waiting for PR merge HealthChecking Checking health Verifying Verifying Verified Live Failed Failed AbortedByAlarm Stopped by alarm RollingBack Rolling back Superseded Replaced by newer version

An environment whose step waits for a gate is shown as "Held by gate ", and one held on a rolled-back version as "Held by rollback".

docs.title: Sub-step
docs.text:
The steps inside a promotion step (status.steps[]: git-clone, open-pr, health-check, ...).

API value Shown as Pending Not started InProgress In progress Completed Done Failed Failed

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: API value Shown as Pending Not evaluated yet Waiting Not ready Pass Passing Block Blocking Superseded Replaced by newer version Rejected Version rejected

docs.title: Helm values
docs.text:
Every value of the kardinal-promoter chart, with its default. Set them with --set or a values file; the chart's schema rejects an unknown key. The descriptions are the comments in values.yaml. Where a value sets a controller flag, the flag is in Controller flags.

Key Default Description replicaCount 1 Number of controller replicas terminationGracePeriodSeconds 60 Pod termination grace period in seconds. Keep it above shutdownDelaySeconds plus the controller's 30s shutdown timeout: on SIGTERM the controller gives in-flight HTTP requests up to 20s, then cancels in-flight reconciles, and exits within 30s. shutdownDelaySeconds 5 Seconds a controller Pod being deleted keeps serving before it gets SIGTERM (a preStop sleep). Services stop sending it new connections meanwhile, so a rollout or a node drain does not refuse or drop UI, webhook and Bundle API requests. It counts against terminationGracePeriodSeconds. 0 sends SIGTERM at once. image.repository ghcr.io/pnz1990/kardinal-promoter/controller Container image repository image.pullPolicy IfNotPresent Image pull policy image.tag "" Image tag (defaults to chart appVersion) image.digest "" Image digest (sha256:...); when set the image is repository@digest and the tag is not used. imagePullSecrets [] Image pull secrets for private registries. The render Jobs get them too (--render-image-pull-secrets); they must exist in the Pipeline namespaces. nameOverride "" Override the name of the chart fullnameOverride "" Override the full name of the chart serviceAccount.create true Create a ServiceAccount serviceAccount.annotations {} Annotations to add to the ServiceAccount serviceAccount.name "" Override the ServiceAccount name podAnnotations {} Annotations to add to the controller Pod podSecurityContext {"runAsNonRoot":true,"seccompProfile":{"type":"RuntimeDefault"}} Security context for the controller Pod securityContext {"allowPrivilegeEscalation":false,"capabilities":{"drop":["ALL"]},"readOnlyRootFilesystem":true,"runAsNonRoot":true} Security context for the controller container logLevel info Controller log level: debug, info, warn or error. Sets both the reconciler logger (--log-level) and controller-runtime's logger (--zap-log-level; warn maps to error there, which has no warn level). leaderElect true Enable leader election for controller manager leaderElectionFlowSchema.enabled true Create the FlowSchema. leaderElectionFlowSchema.matchingPrecedence 90 Its matchingPrecedence. It must be lower (matched first) than any FlowSchema that matches the controller's other requests; the built-in workload ones are 9000 and above. leaderElectionFlowSchema.priorityLevel leader-election The priority level the Lease requests use. controller.tlsCertFile "" Path to the TLS certificate file (PEM). Set together with tlsKeyFile to enable TLS. controller.tlsKeyFile "" Path to the TLS private key file (PEM). Set together with tlsCertFile to enable TLS. controller.watchNamespace "" Namespace-scoped install mode (--watch-namespace). Empty = cluster-wide. When set, the controller caches and reconciles only this namespace, its namespaced permissions are a Role/RoleBinding there, and a small ClusterRole (<fullname>-cluster-scoped) covers ChangeWindows and get on this Namespace. It must equal the release namespace (install the chart into the namespace it watches); org-level PolicyGates are read from this namespace too. controller.namespaceShard "" Controller shard (--namespace-shard). Empty = no sharding: this controller reconciles every namespace. Set, it reconciles the namespaces labelled kardinal.io/shard=<name>; "default" also takes the namespaces without the label and the cluster-scoped kinds. Install one release per shard (one of them "default"), each in its own namespace labelled with its shard. Grants list/watch on Namespaces and Leases cluster-wide: each shard holds a Lease kardinal-shard in every namespace it reconciles. Cannot be combined with watchNamespace. See docs/sharding.md. controller.policyNamespaces [] Namespaces holding org-level PolicyGates (--policy-namespaces). Empty keeps the controller default, platform-policies. In namespace mode org gates are read from watchNamespace, and an entry other than watchNamespace fails the install. controller.gateStatusHeartbeat "" Longest a PolicyGate's status goes unwritten while its result does not change (--gate-status-heartbeat, a Go duration). Empty keeps the controller default, 10m. "0s" writes the status on every evaluation; each write makes kro re-check the gate's whole Graph. controller.workers {} Workers per controller: how many objects of a kind are reconciled at once (--promotionstep-workers, ...). One object is never reconciled twice at once. Unset keeps the controller defaults, measured with the scale suite: promotionStep 16, prStatus 8, policyGate 8, bundle 4, pipeline 4. Raise promotionStep for many Pipelines on slow git hosts. See docs/operate.md (Controller concurrency). controller.accessLog Access log of the UI API and the Bundle API: logins (TokenReviews), refusals (401/403/429, with the reason) and writes are always logged as structured lines (component=access). Tokens are never logged. controller.accessLog.allRequests false Log every request (--access-log-all-requests). controller.accessLog.sourceIP false Add the client address (--access-log-source-ip). controller.accessLog.trustedProxies [] CIDRs of proxies (an Ingress controller) whose X-Forwarded-For gives the client address (--access-log-trusted-proxies). Other clients' X-Forwarded-For is ignored. controller.gateOverrideMaxMinutes "" Longest a gate override counts, in minutes from when the controller first saw it (--gate-override-max-minutes): an override ends at the earlier of its expiresAt and this cap. Empty keeps the default, 1440 (24h). controller.extraArgs [] Extra controller args, e.g. ["--cors-allowed-origins=https://kardinal.example.com"]. controller.extraEnv [] Extra env vars for the controller container (e.g. HTTPS_PROXY). controller.extraVolumes [] Extra volumes for the controller Pod (e.g. a TLS Secret). controller.extraVolumeMounts [] Extra volume mounts for the controller container. metricsBindAddress :8080 Address the metrics endpoint binds to healthProbeBindAddress :8081 Address the health probe endpoint binds to pprofAddress "" Address that serves Go pprof profiles under /debug/pprof/ (--pprof-address). Empty (the default) serves none. An address without a host, such as ":6060", binds to 127.0.0.1: reach it with kubectl port-forward. The profiles show heap contents, so no Service or container port exposes it. It has no authentication, and /debug/pprof/cmdline shows the process args: keep secrets out of controller.extraArgs. service.metricsPort 8080 Metrics port (Prometheus) service.healthPort 8081 Health/readiness probe port service.uiPort 8082 Embedded UI and UI API port (--ui-listen-address) service.webhookPort 8083 Webhook and Bundle API port (--webhook-bind-address): /webhook/scm and /api/v1/bundles resources {"limits":{"cpu":"500m","memory":"1Gi"},"requests":{"cpu":"10m","memory":"256Mi"}} Controller resources. The controller caches every Pipeline, Bundle, PromotionStep, PRStatus and PolicyGate it watches, so its memory grows with Pipelines times the Bundle history. Measured peaks (scale suite): 166 MiB for 200 Pipelines with a Bundle each, 409 MiB for 2 Bundles a second over 40 Pipelines with leader kills; 55-70 MiB with no Pipelines. The defaults give the larger load 2.5x headroom; see "Sizing the controller" in docs/operate.md. nodeSelector {} Node selector for the controller Pod tolerations [] Tolerations for the controller Pod affinity {} Affinity rules for the controller Pod github github.token and github.secretRef are the old names of scm.token and scm.secretRef (below) and keep working, for every scm.provider. Setting both names to different values fails the install. github.token "" Old name of scm.token. github.secretRef Old name of scm.secretRef. github.secretRef.name "" Old name of scm.secretRef.name. github.secretRef.namespace "" Old name of scm.secretRef.namespace. github.secretRef.key "" Empty is "token". github.app {"enabled":false} Authenticate as a GitHub App: the scm.secretRef Secret holds githubAppID, githubAppInstallationID and githubAppPrivateKey instead of a token. The controller mints installation tokens, refreshes them before they expire, and reloads the App credentials when the Secret changes. Needs scm.provider github (or empty) and scm.secretRef.name. admission SCM provider (--scm-provider): github (default when empty), gitlab, forgejo, gitea, bitbucket, azuredevops or bitbucket-datacenter, and its API base URL (--scm-api-url) for self-hosted instances. See docs/scm-providers.md. Identity admission policies (templates/identity-admission.yaml, docs/guides/security.md#verified-identity). admission.controllerUsernames [] Usernames, besides this release's controller ServiceAccount, that run a kardinal controller: they may name any Bundle's kardinal.io/created-by, write the objects a promotion Graph manages, and record or revoke the UI's Approvals (kardinal.io/recorded-via: ui). Exact usernames only, for example "system:serviceaccount:kardinal-system:kardinal-promoter-b"; there are no wildcards. Never list a ServiceAccount of a tenant's namespace: whoever can mint tokens for a listed ServiceAccount passes these checks. scm.provider "" SCM provider (--scm-provider): github (default when empty), gitlab, forgejo, gitea, bitbucket, azuredevops or bitbucket-datacenter. A Pipeline can name another with spec.git.providerRef. See docs/scm-providers.md. scm.apiURL "" API base URL of a self-hosted SCM (--scm-api-url); empty: the provider's public API. scm.token "" SCM token for scm.provider, for opening PRs and detecting merges. Set one of: Either way the controller reads GITHUB_TOKEN from the Secret and watches it, reloading the SCM provider when the token changes (no restart). Never label this Secret kardinal.io/referenceable, and never name it in a Pipeline's git.secretRef (the controller refuses that): see demo.secretRef for the demo Pipeline's own Secret, and docs/guides/security.md. scm.secretRef Existing Secret holding the token. scm.secretRef.name "" Name of an existing Secret in the release namespace that holds the SCM token (or the GitHub App credentials with github.app.enabled). scm.secretRef.namespace "" Must be empty or the release namespace: GITHUB_TOKEN is read with a secretKeyRef, which only reads the Pod's namespace. scm.secretRef.key "" Key of the token in the Secret. Empty is "token". scm.allowedRepositories [] Repositories the controller's SCM token may act on (--scm-allowed-repositories), as host/repository globs: "github.com/acme/", "gitlab.example.com/platform/" for every subgroup, "dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/" for Azure DevOps. Every SCM call for another repository is refused, and a Pipeline that would need the token for one is Ready=False/RepositoryNotAllowed with its steps failing before git-clone (exempt: its own existing git.secretRef Secret and no pr-review environment). Empty allows every repository the token can write to, and the controller logs a warning at startup. See docs/guides/security.md. scm.providersAllowInsecureHTTP false Let ScmProviders and ClusterScmProviders use an http:// spec.apiURL (--scm-providers-allow-http), for an in-cluster SCM without TLS. Off, a provider must use https://, so its token never crosses the network in clear text. Their API requests always go through the egress guard (no loopback, link-local or cloud metadata addresses). scm.instanceSigners [] Forgejo/Gitea only: the names or emails the instance signs commits with (its repository.signing SIGNING_NAME / SIGNING_EMAIL, --scm-instance-signers). Image verification treats such a commit as a platform signature (forgejo-instance). Without it, a verified signer that is not a user of the instance is taken as the instance key. scm.gatesCommitStatus {"context":"kardinal/gates","enabled":true} The gate results of a waiting pr-review step as a commit status on the commit kardinal pushed to its PR (docs/pr-evidence.md). enabled: false (--gates-commit-status=false) posts none, for a token without the commit-status permission. context (--gates-status-context) is the status name branch protection requires; it is reserved for kardinal. webhook {"secretRef":{"key":"secret","name":""}} Webhook secret for :8083/webhook/scm (KARDINAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET): the HMAC key, or for GitLab and Azure DevOps the plain token the SCM sends. bundleAPI Bearer token for the Bundle API, POST :8083/api/v1/bundles (KARDINAL_BUNDLE_TOKEN). The Bundle API is off until this is set. bundleAPI.tokenSecretRef.name "" Name of a Secret in the release namespace holding the Bundle API bearer token (KARDINAL_BUNDLE_TOKEN). The Bundle API is off until a token or tokenReview is set. bundleAPI.tokenSecretRef.key token Key of the token in that Secret. bundleAPI.tokenReview false Accept Kubernetes tokens on POST /api/v1/bundles (--bundle-api-tokenreview-auth): each caller is authenticated with a TokenReview and needs create on bundles (and get on the Pipeline) in the namespace, e.g. the promoter role. The static token, when set, still works as a single-tenant admin token. tokenReview TokenReview settings shared by ui.auth.tokenReview and bundleAPI.tokenReview. tokenReview.audiences ["kardinal-promoter"] Token audiences accepted (--tokenreview-audiences). Mint a token for kardinal with: kubectl create token <sa> --audience kardinal-promoter. Such a token is refused by the API server itself, so kardinal cannot replay it there. At least one, unless acceptAPIServerAudience is set. tokenReview.acceptAPIServerAudience false Also accept tokens for the API server's own audience (--tokenreview-accept-apiserver-audience): kubeconfig tokens and default ServiceAccount tokens. Such a token also works against the API server, so whoever holds kardinal's traffic can use it there; opt in knowingly. ui Embedded UI (:8082). ui.corsAllowedOrigins [] Origins allowed by CORS on the UI API (--cors-allowed-origins). ui.allowedHosts [] Extra host names the UI answers to (--ui-allowed-hosts), for example an Ingress host or a node IP. The Service DNS names (<fullname>, <fullname>.<namespace>, .svc and .svc.cluster.local) and localhost are always allowed. Browser requests to any other Host get no same-origin grant, and while UI auth is off every UI API request to them, reads included, gets 403 (DNS rebinding protection). Static /ui/ assets are not checked. Host names only: no scheme, path or wildcard. ui.auth.tokenSecretRef {"key":"token","name":""} Static bearer token for /api/v1/ui/* (KARDINAL_UI_TOKEN). ui.auth.tokenReview false Validate UI bearer tokens as Kubernetes ServiceAccount/user tokens (--ui-tokenreview-auth). Adds tokenreviews and subjectaccessreviews create to the controller's ClusterRole. ui.auth.allowStaticTokenWithTokenReview false Install even when tokenSecretRef.name and tokenReview are both set (--ui-auth-static-overrides-tokenreview). The static token then wins and every UI caller acts as the controller, so by default that combination fails the install. health Health checks of the PromotionSteps. health.refresh.enabled true Ask the GitOps tool to sync a promotion's commit as soon as it is in git (--health-refresh), once per step, instead of waiting for its poll (Argo CD: 3 minutes by default): argocd.argoproj.io/refresh on the Application of health.type argocd, reconcile.fluxcd.io/requestedAt on the Kustomization of health.type flux and its GitRepository. Grants patch on argoproj.io Applications, Flux Kustomizations and GitRepositories; the <fullname>-gitops-writes admission policy denies the controller any change to them but that annotation unless it may update the object. An environment's health.refresh: false turns it off there. See docs/health-adapters.md#sync-on-promotion. rbac Optional controller permissions, off by default. rbac.argocdApplicationsWrite false patch and update on argoproj.io Applications, for the argocd update strategy (update.strategy: argocd). update is what lets the controller change an Application's spec past the gitops-writes admission policy, which otherwise allows only the refresh annotation (health.refresh). rbac.userRoles.enabled true ClusterRoles for users and automation: <fullname>-viewer, -promoter, -approver and -admin (templates/user-roles.yaml). Bind them per namespace with RoleBindings. See docs/guides/security.md#user-roles. rbac.userRoles.aggregateToDefaultRoles false Also aggregate them into the built-in view (viewer), edit (promoter, approver) and admin ClusterRoles. Off by default: with it, everyone bound to edit can both promote and approve gates in that namespace. rbac.userRoles.directWrites false Also grant the promoter update on Pipelines and the approver update on PolicyGates, so kardinal pause, kardinal rollback --hold, kardinal unhold and kardinal override work from their kubeconfigs. An admission policy limits those writes to spec.paused and spec.holds (Pipelines; the hold-writes policy checks each hold entry) and spec.overrides (PolicyGates). Off: they act through the UI API only. On weakens the audit trail: those writes are the user's own, with no requested-by record from kardinal, and createdBy is checked only by the policy. graph kro Graph integration. kardinal renders one kro Graph (kro.run/v1alpha1) per Bundle. kro v0.10.0-rc.0 or later with the GraphKind feature gate must be installed separately: kro applies each Graph's children by impersonating graph.serviceAccountName in the Graph's namespace; the controller creates that ServiceAccount and binds it to the ClusterRoles below with RoleBindings. graph.serviceAccountName kardinal-graph ServiceAccount kro impersonates for each Graph. graph.kroNamespace kro-system Namespace kro runs in. Only used for a NetworkPolicy egress rule; "" drops that rule. graph.readerNamespaces ["argocd","flux-system"] Namespaces, besides a Graph's own namespace, where the controller may bind the Graph ServiceAccount to the reader ClusterRole so the Graph can read health objects (Argo CD Applications, Flux Kustomizations, Deployments). A health check in any other namespace gets no Graph ref and a warning; the PromotionStep health check itself is unaffected. "*" allows every namespace except kube-system, kube-public and kube-node-lease: use it only when every Pipeline author may read every namespace. graph.aggregateToKro true Ship a ClusterRole aggregated into kro's controller role, for kro installed with rbac.mode=aggregation (the hack/install-kro.sh default). graph.compactAbove null Environment count above which a Bundle's Graph uses the compact shape (--graph-compact-above): one PromotionStep collection instead of one node per environment. null keeps the controller default, 100; 0 makes every Graph compact. A Pipeline's kardinal.io/graph-shape annotation overrides it. graph.retire When the Graph of a finished Bundle is retired: deleted, with the Bundle's PromotionSteps kept in status.retiredSteps. kro holds every Graph in memory (3 to 6 MB each), so keeping the Graph of every finished Bundle until spec.historyLimit prunes it runs kro out of memory. Go durations; empty keeps the controller default; "0s" keeps those Graphs. A Pipeline's kardinal.io/graph-retire-after annotation replaces all three for its Bundles. See docs/operate.md#sizing-kro. graph.retire.superseded "" A Superseded Bundle, or a Verified one that a newer Bundle replaced in every environment (--graph-retire-superseded-after, default 1m). graph.retire.failed "" A Failed Bundle (--graph-retire-failed-after, default 24h). A retired Failed Bundle does not recover. graph.retire.verified "" A Verified Bundle still deployed in an environment (--graph-retire-verified-after, default 1h). hooks Pipeline pre- and post-deploy hooks (spec.environments[].hooks, docs/hooks.md). The controller runs each hook as a Job in the Pipeline namespace. hooks.serviceAccounts ["default"] ServiceAccount names a hook's Job Pod may run as (--hook-service-accounts), in the Pipeline namespace. A hook whose Pod names another one fails without running. Anyone who can edit a Pipeline can run a Pod as one of these, so list only ServiceAccounts with the rights a hook needs. The Graph ServiceAccount (graph.serviceAccountName) is never allowed. hooks.podSecurityLevel baseline Pod Security Standard a hook's Pod must meet (--hook-pod-security-level): baseline (no privileged containers, host namespaces, hostPath volumes, added capabilities beyond the baseline set...), restricted (also non-root, no privilege escalation, seccomp RuntimeDefault, all capabilities dropped), or privileged (no Pod checks). Below privileged, nodeName and hostPort are refused too. A hook that breaks it fails without running. render Rendered manifests (layout: branch, docs/rendered-manifests.md). Each render runs as a Job in the Pipeline's namespace from this image, never in the controller: no Kubernetes credentials (the ServiceAccount below gets no role and no token), a read-only root filesystem, no capabilities, and these limits. It reads the DRY source and pushes the render with the Pipeline's own git Secret (spec.git.secretRef). render.image.repository ghcr.io/pnz1990/kardinal-promoter/render kardinal-render image repository. render.image.tag "" Tag (defaults to chart appVersion). render.image.digest "" Digest (sha256:...); when set the image is repository@digest and the tag is not used. render.image.pullPolicy "" imagePullPolicy of the render Jobs (empty: Kubernetes' default). render.serviceAccountName kardinal-render ServiceAccount the render Pods run as. The controller creates it in a Pipeline namespace that has none, without a token; bind no role to it. render.resources.limits.cpu 1 CPU limit of a render Job. render.resources.limits.memory 512Mi Memory limit of a render Job. A render that needs more fails. render.timeout 5m How long a render Job may run. render.networkPolicy NetworkPolicy for the render Pods: egress only to DNS and the git host. Needs a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy. It is created in each of namespaces (the Pipeline namespaces that use layout: branch). render.networkPolicy.enabled false Create the render NetworkPolicy. render.networkPolicy.namespaces [] Namespaces to create the render NetworkPolicy in. render.networkPolicy.gitEgress [] Egress rules (NetworkPolicyPeer lists with ports) for the git host, e.g. [{to: [{ipBlock: {cidr: 140.82.112.0/20}}], ports: [{port: 443, protocol: TCP}]}]. tracing.enabled false Export OpenTelemetry traces over OTLP/HTTP (--tracing-enabled): spans for reconciles, promotion steps, git clone/push, SCM API calls and NotificationHook deliveries (which carry a traceparent header), and server spans for /webhook/scm and /api/v1/bundles. See docs/guides/monitoring.md. tracing.endpoint "" OTLP/HTTP endpoint: a URL (http://otel-collector.observability:4318) or host:port. Empty uses OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (set it with controller.extraEnv), else localhost:4318. tracing.insecure false Plain HTTP to a host:port endpoint (a URL's scheme decides by itself). tracing.samplingRatio 0.1 Fraction of traces recorded, 0 to 1, decided at each trace's root. An inbound traceparent is linked, not trusted, so it does not force recording. egress.allowlist [] Destinations NotificationHook, MetricCheck and Subscription requests may reach (--egress-allowlist): host names (hooks.slack.com), wildcards (*.example.com: any name under it) and CIDRs or addresses (10.0.0.0/8). A request is allowed when its host matches a name or every address it connects to is in a CIDR. Empty: any destination except loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, unspecified and multicast addresses, which stay refused whatever this lists. See docs/guides/security.md. networkPolicy NetworkPolicy for the controller Pod. Needs a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy. Egress: DNS, :443/:6443 (API server, SCM, git, registries), graph.kroNamespace and extraEgress. Ingress: the four Service ports. networkPolicy.enabled false Create the controller NetworkPolicy. networkPolicy.ingressFrom {"health":[],"metrics":[],"ui":[],"webhook":[]} Peers allowed per ingress port (NetworkPolicyPeer list). Empty admits any source on that port. Example: networkPolicy.extraEgress [] Extra egress rules (NetworkPolicyEgressRule list), e.g. Prometheus on :9090 for MetricChecks or a webhook receiver for NotificationHooks. audit AuditEvent retention, on by default. AuditEvents have no owner, so without retention they stay in etcd for ever, and a full etcd quota stops the whole cluster. The leader deletes, every 10 minutes, the records older than maxAge and, per Pipeline, all but the maxPerPipeline newest (records that name no Pipeline share one cap per namespace), at most 2000 a run at 5 API requests a second; the chart grants the controller delete on AuditEvents. enabled: false keeps every record. Upgrading deletes the records already past these limits: export them first if you must keep them. See docs/guides/security.md (Retention). audit.retention.enabled true Delete AuditEvents past maxAge and maxPerPipeline (--audit-retention). false keeps every record. audit.retention.maxAge 2160h Delete records created longer ago than this (--audit-retention-max-age, a Go duration). "0s" keeps records of any age. audit.retention.maxPerPipeline 1000 Keep this many newest records per Pipeline (--audit-retention-max-per-pipeline). 0 keeps any number. A gate that flips often writes a record per flip and reaches it quickly. A record created in the last 10 minutes is kept even past it. metricCheck MetricCheck providers. metricCheck.cloudWatch.ambientCredentials false Let cloudwatch MetricChecks that name no credential Secret use the controller's own AWS identity (IRSA, EKS Pod Identity, environment). Off by default: anyone who can create a MetricCheck could then read CloudWatch with that identity. Annotate serviceAccount for IRSA. metricCheck.querySlots {"global":12,"perNamespace":1} Outbound MetricCheck query slots. Every provider dials an address the MetricCheck's author chose, so queries are capped: at most global run at once in the cluster, at most perNamespace per namespace, and the rest wait first come, first served (status reason WaitingForSlot). The sustained throughput is about global / query time: with 12 slots and 0.5 s queries, 24 queries a second, so 1,440 MetricChecks at a 60 s interval. One namespace gets at most perNamespace / query time. The MetricCheck controller runs global + 4 workers (at least 16), so every slot can be used. scheduleClock {"enabled":true,"interval":"1m"} ScheduleClock configuration. One ScheduleClock is deployed per cluster. Each tick re-evaluates every PolicyGate instance, so schedule.* expressions follow the interval; each gate's recheckInterval still applies as well. pdb PodDisruptionBudget for the controller. Only created when replicaCount > 1 to ensure at least one replica is available during node maintenance or rolling updates. pdb.enabled true Create the PodDisruptionBudget (only when replicaCount > 1). pdb.minAvailable 1 Minimum number of pods that must be available during disruption. topologySpread {"enabled":true} Topology spread constraints for multi-replica deployments. When enabled and replicaCount > 1, prefers spreading replicas across zones (topology.kubernetes.io/zone, whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway). It does not stop two replicas from sharing a node. demo Demo mode — pre-installs a ready-to-use Pipeline targeting the kardinal-demo reference GitOps repository (pnz1990/kardinal-demo). When enabled, a demo Pipeline CR is created in the release namespace with three environments (test, uat, prod) and kustomize update strategy. Use kardinal create bundle demo --image <image> to trigger the first promotion. Time to first promotion with demo.enabled=true: under 10 minutes on a fresh kind cluster. It needs a fork of pnz1990/kardinal-demo (set demo.git.url) and Argo CD Applications kardinal-test-app-test, -uat and -prod; see docs/quickstart.md. Example: demo.enabled false Enable the demo Pipeline. When true, a Pipeline named "demo" is created. demo.image ghcr.io/pnz1990/kardinal-test-app:sha-DEMO Image tag used in the demo pipeline documentation. This is informational only (shown in the demo Pipeline annotations). Run kardinal create bundle demo --image <real-image> to start a promotion. demo.secretRef {"name":""} Secret the demo Pipeline uses for git (spec.git.secretRef), labelled kardinal.io/referenceable=true. Never the controller's SCM token Secret: the install fails if it is. When empty: with scm.token the chart creates <fullname>-demo-git-token, a labelled copy of the token; else "github-token". demo.git.url https://github.com/pnz1990/kardinal-demo GitOps repository the demo Pipeline pushes to (spec.git.url). The token needs write access to it, so point this at your fork of pnz1990/kardinal-demo. prometheusRule PrometheusRule for Prometheus Operator. Creates a PrometheusRule CR with pre-built alerting rules for kardinal-promoter. Requires the Prometheus Operator CRD (monitoring.coreos.com/v1/PrometheusRule). Disabled by default — enable when using kube-prometheus-stack or similar. prometheusRule.enabled false Create the PrometheusRule resource. Requires Prometheus Operator CRD. prometheusRule.additionalLabels {} Additional labels to add to the PrometheusRule (for Prometheus selector matching). Example: prometheusRule.namespace "" Namespace to deploy the PrometheusRule into. Defaults to Release.Namespace. serviceMonitor ServiceMonitor for Prometheus Operator. Scrapes the controller's metrics port (plain HTTP) through the chart's Service. The job label is the Service name, which is what the PrometheusRule alerts match. Requires the Prometheus Operator CRD (monitoring.coreos.com/v1/ServiceMonitor). Disabled by default — enable when using kube-prometheus-stack or similar. serviceMonitor.enabled false Create the ServiceMonitor resource. Requires Prometheus Operator CRD. serviceMonitor.interval "" Scrape interval, for example "30s". Empty uses the Prometheus default. serviceMonitor.labels {} Additional labels on the ServiceMonitor (for Prometheus selector matching). Example: grafanaDashboard Grafana dashboard ConfigMap for Grafana sidecar auto-discovery. When enabled, creates a ConfigMap containing the kardinal-promoter Grafana dashboard JSON. Designed for use with the Grafana sidecar (grafana.sidecar.dashboards.enabled=true in kube-prometheus-stack or grafana Helm chart). The sidecar watches ConfigMaps labelled with the configured label (default: grafana_dashboard=1) and loads dashboards automatically. Example (kube-prometheus-stack): grafanaDashboard.enabled false Create the Grafana dashboard ConfigMap. grafanaDashboard.sidecarLabel {"grafana_dashboard":"1"} Labels to add to the ConfigMap for Grafana sidecar discovery. Set these to match your Grafana sidecar's label selector. kube-prometheus-stack default: grafana_dashboard: "1" grafanaDashboard.namespace "" Namespace for the dashboard ConfigMap. Defaults to Release.Namespace. grafanaDashboard.annotations {} Annotations to add to the ConfigMap. fleets.applicationNamespaces ["argocd"] Namespaces a fleet selector of kind Application may read Argo CD Applications from (--fleet-application-namespaces). A selector naming another namespace is refused, so a Pipeline author cannot list the Applications of a namespace they cannot read. fleets.clusterProfileNamespaces [] Namespaces, besides the Pipeline's own, a fleet selector of kind ClusterProfile may read (--fleet-clusterprofile-namespaces).

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: The controller serves Prometheus metrics on its metrics port. Monitor shows how to scrape them, the sample queries, the alerts and the Grafana dashboard.

docs.title: Controller-Runtime Standard Metrics
docs.text: kardinal-promoter uses controller-runtime, which automatically exposes the following metrics:

docs.title: Reconciler metrics
docs.text:
Metric Type Description controller_runtime_reconcile_total Counter Total reconcile operations, labelled by controller and result (success, error, requeue, requeue_after) controller_runtime_reconcile_errors_total Counter Total reconcile errors, labelled by controller controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds Histogram Time spent per reconcile loop, labelled by controller controller_runtime_max_concurrent_reconciles Gauge Configured max concurrent reconciles per controller controller_runtime_active_workers Gauge Active reconcile goroutines per controller

Controller labels: bundle, changewindow, graphcleanup, metriccheck, notificationhook, pipeline, policygate, promotionstep, prstatus, rollbackpolicy, scheduleclock, subscription

docs.title: Work queue metrics
docs.text: Metric Type Description workqueue_adds_total Counter Items added to the work queue per controller workqueue_depth Gauge Current work queue depth per controller workqueue_queue_duration_seconds Histogram Time items spend in the queue before processing workqueue_work_duration_seconds Histogram Time spent processing each item workqueue_retries_total Counter Total retries per controller

docs.title: kardinal Metrics
docs.text:
The controller registers these on the same /metrics endpoint (pkg/reconciler/observability/metrics.go):

Metric Type Labels Description kardinal_bundles_total Counter phase Bundle phase transitions, labelled by the phase entered kardinal_steps_total Counter type (always PromotionStep), result (succeeded, failed) PromotionSteps reaching a terminal state kardinal_gate_evaluations_total Counter result (allowed, blocked) PolicyGate evaluations kardinal_api_access_log_dropped_total Counter kind (denied, request) API access log lines not written over their per-second budget (API access log) kardinal_audit_write_failures_total Counter kind (PromotionStep, PolicyGate, Pipeline) AuditEvent creates that failed and stay in the writer's status.pendingAuditEvents to be retried (Audit outbox). While a finished Bundle's step or gate holds unwritten records, its Graph is not retired: the Bundle's GraphRetired condition stays Unknown (reason WaitingForSteps) and names the object, so a counter that keeps rising with Bundles stuck there means the outbox cannot drain kardinal_audit_events_dropped_total Counter kind, reason (overflow, invalid) Audit records never written: the outbox of 32 was full, or the API server rejected the record. Alert on any increase kardinal_pr_duration_seconds Histogram — Time from the PR opening (the open-pr step completing) to the merge the controller sees, observed once, when the step's move to HealthChecking is written kardinal_step_duration_seconds Histogram step (step name, e.g. git-clone) Duration of each promotion step, observed once, when the status that records it Completed or Failed is written. wait-for-merge lasts until the merge; health-check covers the health check and the bake kardinal_gate_blocking_duration_seconds Histogram — How long a PolicyGate was blocked before it allowed kardinal_promotionstep_age_seconds Histogram — PromotionStep age when it reaches a terminal state kardinal_auditevents_pruned_total Counter — AuditEvents deleted by retention (audit.retention) kardinal_events_dropped_total Counter recorder, type Kubernetes Events not written because the controller was over its rate: type="Normal" over --event-qps/--event-burst, type="Warning" over a namespace's --event-warning-qps/--event-warning-burst (Kubernetes Events lists each Warning's durable record) kardinal_pr_cleanup_failures_total Counter reason Deleted PromotionSteps whose PR the controller left open (PRLeftOpen) or could not close (ClosePRFailed): close those PRs by hand, since merging one changes an environment with no step tracking it (Troubleshooting) kardinal_hold_bundle_missing_total Counter pipeline_namespace, pipeline Holds whose rollback Bundle has been missing for --hold-bundle-grace, at most once per hold (the HoldBundleMissing AuditEvent is the durable record). The hold stays in effect until released (A hold whose rollback Bundle does not exist) kardinal_notifications_dropped_total Counter hook_namespace, hook, reason (template, attempts) Events a NotificationHook gave up on without delivering: the body could not be rendered for the event, or the last of 10 delivery attempts failed. Each also emits a Warning Event on the hook (Templated body)

docs.title: SCM API and git metrics
docs.text:
Every call the controller makes to the SCM API (GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo/Gitea, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps) and every git clone and push is measured (pkg/scm/metrics.go):

Metric Type Labels Description kardinal_scm_requests_total Counter provider, owner, operation, result SCM API calls. result is ok, client_error (4xx), server_error (5xx), rate_limited (quota used up: 429, or 403 with Retry-After or no remaining quota), network_error (no response) or circuit_open (refused by the circuit breaker before any call) kardinal_scm_request_duration_seconds Histogram provider, operation Latency of the calls that were made, including reading the response kardinal_scm_rate_limit_remaining Gauge provider, owner What is left in the rate-limit window, from the last response's X-RateLimit-Remaining or RateLimit-Remaining header. Absent until a response carries one (see below) kardinal_scm_rate_limit_limit Gauge provider, owner The window's size (X-RateLimit-Limit / RateLimit-Limit) kardinal_scm_rate_limit_reset_timestamp_seconds Gauge provider, owner When the window resets, as a Unix time (X-RateLimit-Reset / RateLimit-Reset) kardinal_scm_circuit_state Gauge provider, owner Circuit breaker state: 0 closed, 1 half-open (one probe allowed), 2 open (calls refused). owner="_quota" is the circuit that opens when the token's rate limit is used up kardinal_git_operations_total Counter operation (clone, push), result (ok, error, non_fast_forward) Git clones and pushes. non_fast_forward is a push that lost to another writer of the branch (it is rebased and retried) kardinal_git_operation_duration_seconds Histogram operation Duration of git clones and pushes kardinal_git_transfer_bytes_total Counter git_service (fetch, push), direction (sent, received) Bytes git transferred over HTTP(S). fetch covers clones and fetches (git-upload-pack), push covers git-receive-pack. Git over ssh is not counted

Cardinality is bounded. The owner label is the repository owner (organization, user, top-level GitLab group, Bitbucket workspace or Azure DevOps organization). It is never the repository. An owner gets its own value only after a call for it succeeded (a 2xx response), and only the first 50 such owners do; calls for any other owner, including ones that only ever fail, are reported as _other. Calls without an owner, such as the startup token check, use _none. operation is the HTTP method and the API resource words of the path, for example POST pulls, GET merge_requests or DELETE git refs heads. Names, numbers and SHAs are dropped, and there are at most 100 values. Owner and operation values are cut to 64 bytes. The reserved values _other, _none and _quota start with _. A controller has at most 5 providers × 52 owner values of each owner-labelled series.

What the rate-limit gauges mean depends on the provider and the credential:

  • GitHub sends X-RateLimit-* on every response. With a personal access token the quota belongs to the token, not to the owner: every owner's gauge shows the same window, and it is per owner only in name. With a GitHub App, each installation (and so each organization) has its own window, which is why the gauges carry owner.
  • GitLab sends RateLimit-* when rate limiting is enabled on the instance (it is on gitlab.com). The limit applies to the token's user.
  • Gitea and Forgejo send no rate-limit headers by default (the API is not rate limited unless a proxy in front of it is), so the gauges are absent.
  • Azure DevOps sends X-RateLimit-* only when a request is delayed or close to the limit, and counts in throughput units (TSTUs) over a sliding window, not in requests. Read remaining as usage units left, not calls left.
  • Bitbucket sends none of these headers.

docs.title: Go Runtime Metrics
docs.text:
Standard Go runtime metrics are also exposed:

Metric Description go_goroutines Current goroutine count go_memstats_alloc_bytes Heap memory in use go_gc_duration_seconds GC pause duration process_cpu_seconds_total CPU time consumed

docs.title: Pipeline field reference
docs.text: Every field of the Pipeline CRD, with its default and behaviour. For how to combine them, see Design a pipeline; the generated CRD API lists the same fields from the Go types.

docs.title: Full Spec
docs.text:
apiVersion: kardinal.io/v1alpha1
kind: Pipeline
metadata:
  name: <string>                        # Pipeline name, typically matches the application
  namespace: <string>                   # Kubernetes namespace
spec:
  git:                                  # Git repository configuration
    url: <string>                       # GitOps repo URL (HTTPS)
    branch: <string>                    # Base branch (default: "main")
    layout: <string>                    # "directory" (default) or "branch" (rendered manifests)
    secretRef:
      name: <string>                    # Secret containing the Git token
      namespace: <string>               # Must be empty or the Pipeline's namespace

  environments:                         # Ordered list of environments
    - name: <string>                    # Environment name (must be unique within the Pipeline)
      path: <string>                    # Path in the GitOps repo (default: "environments/<name>")
      dependsOn: [<string>, ...]        # Environments this one depends on (default: previous in list)
      wave: <int>                       # Deployment wave, minimum 1 (default: none)
      update:
        strategy: <string>              # "kustomize" (default), "helm", "argocd" or "yaml"
        helm:                           # When strategy: helm
          imagePathTemplate: <string>   # Dot path of the image tag (default: ".image.tag")
          valuesFile: <string>          # Relative to path (default: "values.yaml")
          chartVersionFile: <string>    # chart Bundles: file with the chart version (default: "Chart.yaml")
          chartVersionPath: <string>    # chart Bundles: its dot path (default: ".dependencies[name=<chart>].version")
        argocd:                         # When strategy: argocd
          application: <string>         # Argo CD Application to patch (required)
          namespace: <string>           # Default: "argocd"
          imageKey: <string>            # Key in spec.source.helm.valuesObject (default: "image.tag")
        yaml:                           # When strategy: yaml
          updates:                      # One or more; all are applied in one commit
            - file: <string>            # YAML file relative to path
              path: <string>            # YAML path, e.g. "spec.template.spec.containers[name=app].image"
              image: <string>           # Bundle image repository (optional with one image)
              value: <string>           # tag (default), digest, tagWithDigest, image, imageWithDigest
      approval: <string>                # "auto" (default) or "pr-review"
      health:
        type: <string>                  # "resource" (default), "argocd", "flux", "argoRollouts", "flagger"
        labelSelector: {<key>: <value>} # type: resource only: check every matching Deployment,
                                        # in the namespace named after the environment unless
                                        # resource.namespace is set
        resource:                       # When type: resource
          kind: <string>                # Only "Deployment" is supported
          name: <string>                # Default: Pipeline metadata.name
          namespace: <string>           # Default: environment name
          condition: <string>           # Default: "Available"
        argocd:                         # When type: argocd
          name: <string>                # Default: "<pipeline>-<environment>"
          namespace: <string>           # Default: "argocd"
        flux:                           # When type: flux
          name: <string>                # Default: "<pipeline>-<environment>"
          namespace: <string>           # Default: "flux-system"
        argoRollouts:                   # When type: argoRollouts
          name: <string>                # Default: Pipeline metadata.name
          namespace: <string>           # Default: environment name
        flagger:                        # When type: flagger
          name: <string>                # Default: Pipeline metadata.name
          namespace: <string>           # Default: environment name
        timeout: <duration>             # Health check timeout (default: "10m")
      bake:
        minutes: <int>                  # Contiguous healthy minutes before Verified, minimum 1
        policy: <string>                # "reset-on-alarm" (default) or "fail-on-alarm"
        maxDuration: <duration>         # Deadline for one full window (default: minutes + health.timeout)
      onHealthFailure: <string>         # "none" (default), "abort" or "rollback"
      delivery:
        delegate: <string>              # "none" (default), "argoRollouts" (implemented), "flagger" (implemented)
      layout: <string>                  # "directory" (default) or "branch" (rendered manifests)
      render:                           # layout: branch
        branch: <string>                # Rendered branch (default: "env/<name>")
        onDrift: <string>               # "fail" (default) or "overwrite"
        helm: {releaseName: <string>, namespace: <string>, valuesFiles: [<string>]}
        allowNondeterministic: <bool>   # allow randAlphaNum, uuidv4, now, genCA, ... in Helm templates (default false)
      waitForMergeTimeout: <duration>   # pr-review only: fail the step and close the PR after this (default: wait forever)
      pr:                               # pr-review only: the PR (see PR Evidence, Customising the PR)
        titleTemplate: <template>       #   PR title (default: [kardinal] Promote <bundle> to <env>)
        bodyTemplate: <template>        #   PR body; the evidence sections are template functions
        labels: [<template>, ...]       #   Labels added to the kardinal labels
        reviewers: [<template>, ...]    #   Users asked to review
        teamReviewers: [<template>, ...] #  Teams asked to review
        assignees: [<template>, ...]    #   Users assigned, e.g. "{{ .Bundle.Author }}"
        merge:
          auto: <bool>                  #   Enable the SCM's auto-merge on the PR (default: false)
          allowImmediate: <bool>        #   Merge at once when nothing is pending; skips review (default: false)
          method: <string>              #   "merge" (default), "squash" or "rebase"; needs auto
          commitMessageTemplate: <template> # Merge commit message; needs auto
      stepTimeoutSeconds: <int>         # Per built-in step timeout in seconds, minimum 1 (default: none)

  paused: <bool>                        # Hold every promotion of the Pipeline (default: false)
  maxConcurrentPromotions: <int>        # Bundles promoting at once; 0 is no cap (default: 0)
  policyNamespaces: [<string>, ...]     # Extra namespaces to read PolicyGates from (default: none)
  historyLimit: <int>                   # Number of Bundles to retain (default: 50)

docs.title: spec.git
docs.text: Field Required Default Description url Yes URL of the GitOps repository: HTTPS, or ssh (ssh://git@host/owner/repo.git, git@host:owner/repo.git) with an ssh key in secretRef branch No main Base branch: git-clone checks it out, approval: auto pushes to it, and pr-review PRs target it. The API server sets main when the field is omitted, and the controller also reads an empty value as main. layout No directory directory: environments as directories on one branch. branch: every environment's path is rendered (kustomize build, or helm template for a chart) and committed as plain manifests to its rendered branch; see Rendered Manifests. secretRef.name No secretRef is optional; when it is set, name must be too. Name of a Kubernetes Secret in the Pipeline's namespace containing a token field with a GitHub PAT or GitLab token, GitHub App credentials (githubAppID, githubAppInstallationID, githubAppPrivateKey: git then uses installation tokens, see GitHub App), or for an ssh url the sshPrivateKey and knownHosts keys (SSH git authentication). Needed when the HTTPS remote refuses git without a token (every push to a hosted provider, and the clone of a private repository); not needed for a URL that carries its credentials (an ssh remote needs sshPrivateKey and knownHosts instead). When an HTTPS remote has no token this way (not set, a Secret that does not exist, or one with no token key and no GitHub App credentials), the Pipeline is Ready=False with reason GitCredentialMissing as soon as it is applied, and the message is the command that creates the Secret (Troubleshooting). When the remote refuses git-clone or git-push without a token, the step retries until the Secret exists; the step message says what is missing (see Troubleshooting). Label the Secret kardinal.io/referenceable: "true" (kubectl label secret github-token kardinal.io/referenceable=true): the token goes to the Pipeline's git.url, which the Pipeline's author chooses, so the label records that the Secret's owner allows it. An unlabeled Secret is deprecated: it still works, and the Pipeline has the condition SecretReferenceable=False (reason SecretNotReferenceable); v0.11 refuses it. secretRef.namespace No Pipeline's namespace Must be empty or the Pipeline's own namespace. Any other namespace fails the PromotionStep without reading the Secret, so a Pipeline cannot use another namespace's credentials. The Pipeline's Ready condition is False with reason ValidationFailed, and kardinal validate reports it when the file sets metadata.namespace. providerRef.name No Name of the ScmProvider or ClusterScmProvider whose API and token this Pipeline's PRs use. When providerRef is not set, the controller's --scm-provider is used. The provider is resolved when a Bundle's Graph is built. If it is missing, does not allow the Pipeline's namespace (allowedNamespaces of a ClusterScmProvider), or does not allow the repository (allowedRepositories), the Bundle waits with the reason. providerRef.kind No ScmProvider ScmProvider, in the Pipeline's namespace, or ClusterScmProvider.

docs.title: spec.environments[]
docs.text:
A Pipeline has 1 to 500 environments (see Large Pipelines for what fits in one Bundle's Graph). The CRD rejects, at kubectl apply time:

  • a name that is not a DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters. The name is used as a namespace (resource.namespace default, below) and in object names;
  • two environments with the same name;
  • a name that is reserved in kro Graph node IDs or CEL: bundle, time, api-version, kind, metadata, namespace, spec, status, graph, graphengine, kro, each, item, items, object, self, this, context, and CEL keywords such as true, false, null, in, if, for, let, var, while.

Duration fields (health.timeout, waitForMergeTimeout) must be Go durations such as 30s, 10m or 1h30m; a value like 15 minutes is rejected.

Field Required Default Description name Yes Environment name. Must be unique within the Pipeline. Used in PolicyGate matching (kardinal.io/applies-to label). path No environments/<name> Directory in the GitOps repo containing the environment's manifests. It must be relative and stay inside the repository: absolute paths, .. segments and symlinks that point outside the checkout fail the step. dependsOn No Previous environment List of environment names that must be Verified before this one starts. Default: sequential ordering (each depends on the previous). Specifying dependsOn enables parallel fan-out. fleet No (none) Expands the environment into one environment per target, <name>-<target>, promoted at most fleet.maxConcurrent at a time, and stopped after fleet.maxUnavailable failures. The targets are listed in fleet.targets or picked by fleet.selector from Argo CD Applications or cluster inventory ClusterProfiles. See Fleets. wave No (none) Assigns this environment to a numbered deployment wave. Minimum 1. Environments with the same wave number are promoted in parallel. A wave depends on every environment of the next lower wave, and on the environment without a wave listed before it. Gaps in the numbers are allowed. Composable with dependsOn. See Wave Topology. update.strategy No kustomize How to update image references in manifests. kustomize: edits the images: list of the environment's kustomization.yaml the way kustomize edit set image does. helm: patches the image tag at update.helm.imagePathTemplate in update.helm.valuesFile; one image per Bundle, so use one Bundle per chart image, or kustomize. argocd: patches the Argo CD Application's spec.source.helm.valuesObject directly, with no Git commit or PR. The API server rejects argocd with approval: pr-review, and a config or mixed Bundle fails before its first environment when any environment it promotes uses argocd; see Argo CD native promotion. yaml: sets any YAML paths, in any files of the environment directory, to a Bundle image's tag, digest or reference; see The yaml update strategy. update.helm.imagePathTemplate No .image.tag helm only. Dot path of the image tag in the values file. update.helm.valuesFile No values.yaml helm only. Values file to patch, relative to the environment path. update.helm.chartVersionFile No Chart.yaml helm only, for chart Bundles (from a Helm Subscription). File the chart version is written to, relative to the environment path. A chart Bundle fails at build in an environment whose strategy is not helm, or whose layout is branch (the render Job does not get the chart version yet). update.helm.chartVersionPath No .dependencies[name=<chart>].version helm only. YAML path of the chart version in chartVersionFile (.helmCharts[name=podinfo].version, .spec.chart.spec.version, .spec.source.targetRevision). The default is the umbrella chart's dependency named after the Bundle's chart; the step fails when there is none. approval No auto auto: push directly to the target branch, no PR. pr-review: open a PR with promotion evidence, wait for its merge: by a person, or by the SCM with pr.merge.auto. The step list is fixed when an environment's step starts: an edit applies to steps that start after it, so an environment already promoting finishes with the approval it started with and uses the new one from the next Bundle. A step that started as auto still pushes straight to the target branch after an edit to pr-review. The Bundle in flight still finishes: its Graph turns Ready once its steps are Verified and its gates pass, whether or not they opened a PR. health.type No resource Health verification adapter: resource, argocd, flux, argoRollouts or flagger. delivery.delegate, when set, takes precedence. There is no auto-detection. The step is Verified only when the adapter sees the promoted revision (commit or Bundle images) healthy. See Health Adapters. health.resource, health.argocd, health.flux, health.argoRollouts, health.flagger No see Health Check Defaults Name and namespace of the object the adapter checks. health.resource.kind must be Deployment. Without health.resource.namespace, the resource check looks in the namespace named after the environment (environment prod checks namespace prod), not the Pipeline's namespace. health.timeout No 10m Maximum time from the start of health checking to the first healthy check, and from the moment a bake window stops to the next healthy check. When it expires, it counts as a health failure and applies onHealthFailure. It does not cut a running bake window short. health.kubeconfigSecretRef No — {name, key} of a Secret in the Pipeline's namespace holding a kubeconfig (key default kubeconfig). The health check reads its object in that cluster. Inline credentials only; exec, auth-provider and file paths are refused. See Remote Clusters. health.labelSelector No (none) health.type=resource only. When set, every Deployment that matches these labels must pass the health check, in the namespace named after the environment unless health.resource.namespace is set. No match is unhealthy. Example: {"app": "nginx", "kardinal.io/pipeline": "nginx-demo"}. When unset, a single Deployment named after the Pipeline is checked. Ignored for argocd, flux, argoRollouts, and flagger. delivery.delegate No none Progressive delivery delegation. argoRollouts: watch Argo Rollouts Rollout status after promotion. flagger: watch Flagger Canary status. none: instant deploy (rolling update). waitForMergeTimeout No (none) pr-review only. How long the step may wait for its PR to merge, as a Go duration (24h, 72h). When it expires, the step is marked Failed and the controller closes the PR and deletes its head branch (kardinal/<namespace hash>/<bundle>/<env>), so a late merge cannot deliver the change: GitHub's API merges a closed PR whose branch is still there. Unset or 0 waits forever. pr.titleTemplate, pr.bodyTemplate No the default title and body pr-review only. Go templates over the Bundle and the environment that replace the PR title and body; a custom body keeps the evidence sections with the evidence, provenanceTable, gatesTable, upstreamTable and rollbackNotice functions. See Customising the PR. pr.labels, pr.reviewers, pr.teamReviewers, pr.assignees No (none) pr-review only. Up to 20 templates each; every line a template renders is one label, reviewer, team or assignee. Which providers apply which list: PR controls. pr.merge.auto No false pr-review only. Enable the SCM's auto-merge on the PR after it is opened: the SCM merges it once the required checks and reviews pass. kardinal turns it off while the Pipeline is paused or a gate is closed. A PR with nothing pending is left for a merge by hand unless pr.merge.allowImmediate is true, which merges it at once and skips review. pr.merge.method (merge, squash or rebase), pr.merge.commitMessageTemplate and pr.merge.allowImmediate need auto; the API server rejects them without it. See Auto-merge while the step waits. stepTimeoutSeconds No (none) Maximum seconds one built-in step (git-clone, kustomize-set-image, open-pr, ...) may run. The step is cancelled and the error is handled like any other step error: a retryable error is retried with backoff, then the PromotionStep is marked Failed. Minimum 1. Unset means no per-step timeout. bake.minutes No (none) Contiguous-healthy soak window in minutes. When set, the step must observe healthy deployment status continuously for this many minutes before transitioning to Verified. A check that is not healthy stops the window; it starts again at the next healthy check, and health.timeout bounds the wait for it. A Waiting check (the workload is changing, such as a canary paused at a step) is not an alarm under either policy. bake.policy No reset-on-alarm What to do when a check is unhealthy during the bake window. reset-on-alarm: stop the window, increment status.bakeResets, stay in HealthChecking. fail-on-alarm: immediately apply onHealthFailure policy. A release that keeps flapping between healthy and unhealthy fails under reset-on-alarm when no full window completes by the first window's start + bake.minutes + health.timeout (see Timings and failures); fail-on-alarm fails it on the first unhealthy check. bake.maxDuration No bake.minutes + health.timeout Go duration (36h). The longest time from the first bake window's start (status.bakeFirstStartedAt) to a complete window. A window that stops after it, on an alarm or a Waiting check such as a paused canary, applies onHealthFailure.
