A value shorter than bake.minutes counts as bake.minutes. onHealthFailure No none What to do when health.timeout expires without a Healthy result, when the adapter reports a terminal failure (Deployment ProgressDeadlineExceeded from this promotion's rollout, Flagger Failed), or when health fails during bake with policy: fail-on-alarm. none: step → Failed (default behavior). abort: step → AbortedByAlarm; requires human intervention. rollback: create a rollback Bundle with the artifacts of the Bundle verified before the failing one in this environment; step → RollingBack, or AbortedByAlarm when there is nothing safe to roll back to (a step of a rollback Bundle → AbortedByAlarm instead, so rollbacks do not chain). See Automatic Rollback. hooks No (none) Jobs run once per Bundle in this environment: phase: pre before the promotion starts (migrations), phase: post after the health check passed and before the environment is Verified (integration tests). Each is {name, phase, job, timeout}, job a batch/v1 JobSpec. At most 10. A failed pre hook fails the step before it changes anything; a failed post hook applies onHealthFailure. See Pre- and Post-Deploy Hooks. verification No (none) Argo Rollouts analysis after the health check: {analysisTemplates: [{name, kind}], args: [{name, value}], inconclusive, timeout}. One AnalysisRun per template, with the Bundle's tag, image, environment and more as args; the environment is Verified only when every run is Successful, and a failed run applies onHealthFailure. Needs Argo Rollouts installed: without it the Bundle fails. See Analysis.

Reserved and unsupported fields. A health.resource.kind other than Deployment is not implemented: a Bundle fails the environment's step before it changes anything in git. kardinal validate reports it, and the controller sets the Pipeline's Ready condition to False with reason NotImplemented and the same message (kubectl get pipeline <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'). The API server rejects autoRollback outright.

docs.title: spec.historyLimit
docs.text:
Number of finished Bundles (Verified, Failed or Superseded; Rejected Bundles are never deleted) to retain per Pipeline. Older ones are garbage-collected, oldest first, when a new Bundle is created. kardinal rollback can only target a retained Bundle. The Git PR history is permanent regardless of this setting.

Default: 50.

docs.title: spec.paused
docs.text:
When true, no PromotionStep of the Pipeline leaves Pending, and a step in Promoting holds before its next git step. Steps waiting for a PR merge or running a health check finish. The controller keeps a freeze PolicyGate named freeze-<pipeline> while the Pipeline is paused. kardinal pause / kardinal resume and the UI set this field. See Pause and Resume.

Default: false.

docs.title: spec.holds
docs.text:
Environments pinned to a rollback. kardinal rollback --hold (or the UI) writes them, and kardinal unhold (or the UI) removes them. The controller also removes a hold at its expiresAt. Each entry has these fields:

  • environment
  • bundle: the rollback Bundle
  • reason: required, up to 1024 characters
  • createdBy and createdAt
  • expiresAt (optional)
  • artifacts: the digest of the rollback's artifacts when the hold was made

An environment has at most one hold. While it lasts:

  • only bundle promotes into the environment;
  • bundle is never superseded or garbage-collected;
  • if the controller verifies bundle, it passes the environment's PolicyGates, each pass with an EXEMPT reason and audited.

Changing spec.holds needs update on pipelines/hold, and the chart's admission policy pins createdBy to the caller. status.observedHolds is the controller's record, from which it writes the HoldCreated and HoldReleased AuditEvents. See Roll back and hold.

spec:
  holds:
  - environment: prod
    bundle: my-app-rollback-3f9a1c
    reason: "INC-4521: v1.29.0 leaks connections"
    createdBy: alice
    createdAt: "2026-10-09T08:12:00Z"
    expiresAt: "2026-10-10T08:12:00Z"
    artifacts: "sha256:5b0f..."

Default: none.

docs.title: spec.maxConcurrentPromotions
docs.text:
Maximum number of this Pipeline's Bundles in the Promoting phase at once. A Bundle over the cap stays Available with the Ready condition reason WaitingForSlot, and starts when a promoting Bundle becomes Verified, Failed, Superseded or Rejected. 0 means no cap.

A Failed Bundle does not count, so it does not take a slot back while the cap is full. While the cap is full it has the condition WaitingForSlot=True: its Graph creates no new PromotionStep and its Pending steps do not start, so a failed step that is deleted is not recreated until a slot frees. A step that was already running keeps running. When a slot frees the condition is removed, and once nothing is failing the Bundle returns to Promoting. A Failed Bundle that a newer Bundle of its type replaced (one that is Promoting or Verified) is never held: it can only be superseded. A newer Bundle that is still Available does not count, since it may be waiting for the slot too. When several Failed Bundles wait and one slot frees, the hold is lifted on all of them at once, so a step recreated for each can start before the first of them returns to Promoting; the next ones are then held again, but their started steps keep running.

Default: 0.

docs.title: spec.imageVerification
docs.text: Requires the Bundle's images (selected by images, by digest) to carry a signature from one of authorities (a cosign key or a Sigstore keyless identity), and a config Bundle's commit to be signed when commits.requireSigned, before the Bundle is promoted into its first environments. See Image Signature Verification.

docs.title: spec.policyNamespaces
docs.text:
Extra namespaces to read PolicyGates from. It only adds: the org policy namespaces (the controller's --policy-namespaces, default platform-policies) and the Pipeline's namespace are always read. A gate found only through it is a team gate unless it is labelled kardinal.io/scope: org, and it never grants a skip. See Policy Gates.

Default: none.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The Pipeline reconciler writes what runs where onto the Pipeline, so kubectl alone answers it:

$ kubectl get pipelines
NAME     SUMMARY                                                       PHASE       PAUSED   AGE
my-app   1.5.0 live in test, uat; waiting for PR merge in prod (#42)   Promoting   false    3d

$ kubectl get pipelines -o wide      # adds ENVS
ENVS
test=1.5.0 uat=1.5.0 prod=1.4.0

$ kubectl get bundles
NAME          VERSION   TYPE    PIPELINE   PHASE       AGE
my-app-x7k2p  1.5.0     image   my-app     Promoting   12m
Field Meaning status.summary One sentence: each version, its state in words (the labels the CLI and UI use) and the environments it is in. A fleet's targets are counted under the fleet's name, and so are the environments of a wave of more than six (7 of 9 in wave 2): 7.2.0 live in canary and 27 of 42 pops; promoting in 5 pops; queued in 10 pops (the first count of a group gives its size, all 42 pops when that is all of it). Other environments are named, at most six per clause, then N more before any group (e1, …, e6, 2 more and 4 of 10 pops), and so are a clause's PRs. It starts with Not ready (<reason>) when the spec is invalid, and says paused when the Pipeline is paused. A sentence that starts with a version keeps the version's case (sha-9349a3f live in test, main live in test); one that starts with words is capitalised. status.environments[] Per environment, in spec order (a fleet environment lists its targets): bundle and version, what runs there (the newest Bundle whose change landed); incomingBundle and incomingVersion, a newer Bundle on its way in; state, the PromotionStep state of the newest Bundle there (an API value: Verified, WaitingForMerge, …); since, when that state began; blockedBy, the gates holding the newest Bundle back; held, a rollback hold keeps the environment on bundle; prURL, the PR waiting for its merge. status.environmentSummary env=version per environment, - where nothing runs yet: the ENVS column. status.failedVersion When the newest version failed: its bundle and version, the reason and message of the Bundle's InvalidSpec or Failed condition (GraphBuildFailed, GraphRejected, InvalidIntent, StepFailed, …; the message says what fixes it where known), the environment whose step failed (empty when it failed before any step) and since. Cleared once a newer version exists. status.summary adds <version> failed before it started (<reason>) when no environment shows it; kardinal why leads with it and kardinal status <pipeline> prints it as an ERROR line. status.phase The newest Bundle's progress: Ready (Verified everywhere it went), Promoting, Degraded (a version failed) or Unknown (no Bundle yet). Ready condition Whether the spec is valid (reasons Valid, ValidationFailed, NotImplemented, …). It says nothing about promotions: a Ready=True Pipeline can be Degraded.

These fields are for reading: no controller decision uses them. kubectl get kardinal lists the kinds users write (Pipelines, Bundles, PolicyGates, MetricChecks, ChangeWindows, Subscriptions, NotificationHooks, ScmProviders, ClusterScmProviders); kubectl get kardinal-all adds the ones the controller generates (PromotionSteps, PRStatuses, AuditEvents, …).

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
The controller serves two HTTP APIs. Both are described by an OpenAPI 3.1 document, openapi.json, which the controller also serves at GET /api/v1/openapi.json on both listeners (no credentials needed: it holds no data). It is generated from the controller's request and response types, so it always matches the version you run:

kubectl -n kardinal-system port-forward svc/kardinal-promoter 8082:8082 &
curl -s http://localhost:8082/api/v1/openapi.json -o kardinal-openapi.json
# for example: openapi-generator-cli generate -i kardinal-openapi.json -g go -o kardinal-client
API Listener Paths Credentials UI API --ui-listen-address, port 8082 /api/v1/ui/* The UI auth mode: none (loopback only), the shared UI token, or a Kubernetes token with TokenReview Bundle API --webhook-bind-address, port 8083 POST /api/v1/bundles The Bundle API token SCM webhooks port 8083 POST /webhook/scm, GET /webhook/scm/health The webhook secret (signature header), see SCM providers

With controller TLS set (controller.tlsCertFile), both listeners use https://.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Operation GET /api/v1/ui/pipelines List Pipelines with their health, active Bundle and DORA metrics GET /api/v1/ui/pipelines/{pipeline}/bundles List the Bundles of a Pipeline, newest first POST /api/v1/ui/bundles Create an image Bundle GET /api/v1/ui/bundles/{bundle}/graph The promotion DAG of a Bundle GET /api/v1/ui/bundles/{bundle}/steps The PromotionSteps of a Bundle, with per-step timings GET /api/v1/ui/display-states The label, glyph and tone of every Pipeline, Bundle, step and gate state (the words the CLI uses) GET /api/v1/ui/gates List PolicyGates POST /api/v1/ui/gates/{gate}/approve Override a PolicyGate for a while POST /api/v1/ui/gates/{namespace}/{gate}/approve Override a PolicyGate in a namespace for a while POST /api/v1/ui/override Override a gate in one environment of a Pipeline for a while, on its in-progress Bundles' instances (as kardinal override --stage) POST /api/v1/ui/reject Reject a Bundle: it is never promoted again (as kardinal reject) POST /api/v1/ui/promote Promote the Bundle Verified upstream into an environment POST /api/v1/ui/rollback Roll an environment back (with hold, keep it on the rollback) POST /api/v1/ui/release-hold Release the hold of a rollback on an environment POST /api/v1/ui/approvals Approve, reject or revoke a Bundle for an environment's approval gates, as the UI user (TokenReview mode only) POST /api/v1/ui/pause Pause a Pipeline POST /api/v1/ui/resume Resume a Pipeline POST /api/v1/ui/access Which of the given actions the caller may take, and the role that grants each (the UI hides or disables the rest) POST /api/v1/ui/validate-cel Compile a PolicyGate CEL expression GET /api/v1/ui/steps/{namespace}/{step}/events The Kubernetes Events of a PromotionStep POST /api/v1/bundles Create a Bundle from CI (served only when a Bundle API token is set) GET /webhook/scm/health SCM webhook configuration and counters GET /api/v1/openapi.json The OpenAPI description

Errors are text/plain with the HTTP status the OpenAPI document lists for each operation: 400 invalid request, 401 no valid credentials, 403 refused (with no UI auth mode: a client that is not local, or a cross-origin request from an origin not allowed; in TokenReview mode: RBAC denied it), 404 not found (also POST /api/v1/bundles when no Bundle API token is set), 405 wrong method, 409 conflict, 429 rate limited, 503 the TokenReview or SubjectAccessReview API is unreachable (TokenReview mode fails closed). Write endpoints record the caller as the requester (kardinal.io/requested-by on the Bundles they create, createdBy on gate overrides): the Kubernetes user with TokenReview, else kardinal-ui.

POST /api/v1/ui/access answers what the caller may do, so the UI offers only those actions:

{"namespace": "team-a", "checks": [
  {"verb": "create", "resource": "approvals"},
  {"verb": "update", "resource": "pipelines", "subresource": "pause", "name": "checkout"}]}

returns {"user": {"username": "alice", "groups": [...]}, "results": [{"allowed": true, "grantedBy": "approver or admin"}, {"allowed": false, "grantedBy": "promoter or admin"}]}. In TokenReview mode each check is a SubjectAccessReview for the verified caller, cached for 30 seconds like every other check, and a denial is allowed: false, not a 403. Without TokenReview every check is allowed and no user is named, except create approvals: an approval names who decided, so it answers allowed: false with a reason. It answers only for the UI's actions (create bundles, create approvals, update on policygates/override, pipelines/pause, pipelines/hold and bundles/reject), in a namespace that is a DNS-1123 label (the --watch-namespace one when it is set), for names that are DNS-1123 subdomains: anything else is a 400. A request holds at most 32 checks in 16 KiB, and the same check twice is reviewed once. Its SubjectAccessReviews are limited to 300 a minute per user (3,000 for everyone), counted after its cache, as TokenReviews are per client address; past either the answer is 429, saying whether the caller's budget or everyone's ran out. The limit is this endpoint's alone: the checks that authorize UI reads and writes and the Bundle API are not limited, so a flood of /access calls does not lock anyone out of them.

docs.title: API tokens for automation: ServiceAccount tokens
docs.text:
For scripts, bots and dashboards, run the UI API in TokenReview mode (ui.auth.tokenReview=true, see Option 2: Kubernetes tokens) and give each client its own ServiceAccount. The controller validates the token with a TokenReview and authorizes every object the request touches with a SubjectAccessReview for that ServiceAccount, so the client can do through the API exactly what its RBAC allows, and you revoke it like any Kubernetes identity.

  1. Create a ServiceAccount and bind the permissions it needs (the table in Option 2 lists them per action). A read-only dashboard for one team's namespace needs a Role and RoleBinding there:

    apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: release-dashboard
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: kardinal-api-viewer
  namespace: team-a
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["kardinal.io"]
    resources: ["pipelines", "bundles", "policygates", "promotionsteps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["events"]          # step events
    verbs: ["list"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: release-dashboard-kardinal
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: kardinal-api-viewer
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: release-dashboard
    namespace: team-a

    The list endpoints follow namespace RBAC: with a namespaced binding they return the objects of the namespaces the caller may list, and an empty list when there are none. For a dashboard over every team, use the same rules in a ClusterRole bound with a ClusterRoleBinding.

  2. Mint a short-lived token with the TokenRequest API. kubectl create token calls it:

    TOKEN=$(kubectl create token release-dashboard -n team-a --duration=1h --audience kardinal-promoter)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://kardinal.example.com/api/v1/ui/pipelines

    Programs call POST /api/v1/namespaces/team-a/serviceaccounts/release-dashboard/token (client-go: CoreV1().ServiceAccounts("team-a").CreateToken, with spec.audiences: [kardinal-promoter]) and request a new token before status.expirationTimestamp. Inside the cluster, mount a projected ServiceAccount token instead: the kubelet rotates it.

    volumes:
  - name: kardinal-token
    projected:
      sources:
        - serviceAccountToken:
            path: token
            audience: kardinal-promoter
            expirationSeconds: 3600

  3. Use the kardinal-promoter audience (tokenReview.audiences). The controller's TokenReview asks for it and checks the API server returned it, so a token minted for the API server's own audience (a plain kubectl create token, a kubeconfig token) or for anything else is refused with 401. Such a token would also work against the API server; accepting it is the explicit opt-in tokenReview.acceptAPIServerAudience.

To revoke a client, delete its RoleBinding (effective within the 30-second review cache) or its ServiceAccount (its tokens stop validating). Prefer TokenRequest tokens to kubernetes.io/service-account-token Secrets, which never expire.

The shared UI token (ui.auth.tokenSecretRef) is one secret for every caller with full access and no per-caller authorization; use it only behind an authenticating proxy.

docs.title: CI: the Bundle API token
docs.text: POST /api/v1/bundles takes the Bundle API token (bundleAPI.tokenSecretRef, --bundle-api-token), not a Kubernetes token: CI systems outside the cluster can create Bundles without cluster credentials. See CI integration. It is one token shared by every CI caller, limited to 60 requests a minute. A CI job that has cluster credentials can instead create the Bundle with kardinal create bundle or kubectl, authorized by its own RBAC.

docs.title: kardinal approve
docs.text: Approve (or reject) the version waiting for an environment's approval gates

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Record your approval (or, with --decision reject, a rejection) of the version waiting to enter of , in your Kubernetes name; give a Bundle instead with kardinal approve --env . An approval gate passes once enough allowed people approved and nobody rejected. --revoke deletes your Approval.

Creates an Approval object for the Bundle and environment in your name: your Kubernetes username and groups, read from the API server with a SelfSubjectReview (as kubectl auth whoami does). The chart's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy refuses an Approval in anyone else's name.

A PolicyGate with spec.approval on that environment counts the Approvals of the Bundle: it is ready when its expression is true, at least approval.required allowed people (approval.allowedUsers or allowedGroups) approved, and none of them rejected. The gate then lets the environment's PromotionStep start, for approval: auto environments as for pr-review ones. Approving before the Bundle reaches the gate is fine.

--decision reject records a rejection: it blocks the gate. --revoke deletes your Approval for the Bundle and environment.

Running approve again with the same decision does nothing; with another decision it replaces yours. Your Approval is found by its labels and spec.user, not by its name; if the name it would get is taken, the API server generates one. An Approval belongs to its Bundle and is deleted with it. See docs/approvals.md.

kardinal approve <pipeline> <env> [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
kardinal approve my-app prod --comment "checked the canary"

  # a named Bundle, the older form
  kardinal approve my-app-v1-5 --env prod

  # decline (a gate rejection, not kardinal reject)
  kardinal approve my-app prod --decision reject

  # take your decision back
  kardinal approve my-app prod --revoke

docs.text: Aggregate promotion metrics from AuditEvent records

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Summarise promotions from the AuditEvent log over --since: how many, the success rate, the average duration, the gate block rate and the rollbacks.

Rollbacks counts the rollback Bundles created in the window, from kardinal rollback, the UI, a RollbackPolicy or onHealthFailure=rollback, and how many of them succeeded: wrote RollbackSucceeded in the window in the environment they roll back. docs.title: kardinal completion
docs.text: Generate shell completion scripts

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Print the completion script of kardinal for bash, zsh, fish or powershell. Load it in the current shell, or install it permanently (examples below). The bash script needs the bash-completion package.

Tab completes commands and flags, and the names they take, read from the cluster of the current context (-n and --context apply): Pipelines, their environments (the argument after the Pipeline, --env), Bundles with their version and phase (reject, diff, delete bundle, rollback --to, logs --bundle), version tags (approve --version) and gate names (override --gate), in promotion order or newest first, those that start with what is typed. A cluster that cannot be read in 3s (discovery included) completes no names. rollback --to leaves out rejected versions.

The bash script needs the bash-completion package (it calls _get_comp_words_by_ref); install it with your OS package manager first.

To load completions immediately in the current shell session:

# Bash source <(kardinal completion bash)

# Zsh (compinit must be enabled) source <(kardinal completion zsh)

# Fish kardinal completion fish | source

# PowerShell kardinal completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

To install completions permanently:

# Bash (Linux) kardinal completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/kardinal

# Bash (macOS with Homebrew bash-completion@2) kardinal completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/kardinal

# Zsh kardinal completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_kardinal"

# Fish kardinal completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/kardinal.fish

# PowerShell kardinal completion powershell >> $PROFILE

kardinal completion [bash|zsh|fish|powershell]

  kardinal completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/kardinal.fish

docs.title: kardinal create bundle
docs.text: Create a Bundle to trigger promotion through a Pipeline

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Create a Bundle: the version to promote through . An image Bundle needs --image; a config Bundle --config-commit; a mixed one both. --commit, --author and --ci-run-url record its provenance for the PR body and the UI. --dry-run shows the promotion graph and creates nothing.

The pipeline name is a required positional argument; the Pipeline must exist. An image or mixed Bundle needs at least one --image. A config or mixed Bundle needs --config-commit, the commit of the config repository to promote; --config-repo names that repository and defaults to the Pipeline's git.url. An image Bundle with --config-repo or --config-commit is refused: it would deploy only its images and ignore them.

--commit, --author and --ci-run-url set the Bundle's provenance, shown in the PR body and the UI. kardinal records them as given: they are what the caller asserts, as with the Bundle API.

The Bundle API (POST /api/v1/bundles) applies the same checks.

Use --dry-run to preview the promotion graph without creating any resources.

kardinal create bundle <pipeline> [flags]

    --commit abc1234 --author "$GITHUB_ACTOR" --ci-run-url "$RUN_URL"
  kardinal create bundle my-app --type config --config-commit 9f8e7d6

docs.title: kardinal dashboard
docs.text: Open the kardinal UI dashboard in a browser

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Open the kardinal UI (served by the controller at /ui/) in your browser. Without --address it port-forwards a local port (8082 when it is free) to the controller in --controller-namespace, opens the UI and keeps forwarding until Ctrl-C. With --address (or KARDINAL_UI_URL) it opens that URL and forwards nothing. With it opens that pipeline, with its stage.

The UI is served by the controller at /ui/ (port 8082, the Service port named ui). Without --address or KARDINAL_UI_URL, dashboard finds the kardinal-promoter Service with a ui port in --controller-namespace (default kardinal-system) and a ready Pod behind it, forwards 127.0.0.1:8082 (another free port when 8082 is taken) to that Pod, prints the URL, opens it (not with --no-open) and keeps forwarding until Ctrl-C. It needs get on services and endpointslices and create on pods/portforward in that namespace. With --address it prints and opens that URL, and forwards nothing (see "Accessing the UI" in docs/installation.md).

With it opens the UI's page of it (#/p//, the namespace from -n or the kubeconfig context), with that stage's drawer (/env/). kardinal why and kardinal status print the same link on stderr when KARDINAL_UI_URL says where the UI is.

--address and KARDINAL_UI_URL must be http or https URLs with a host, in printable ASCII (punycode a non-ASCII host) and without user@: dashboard refuses another value before it opens anything, and why and status print a warning instead of the link. The url of -o json (create bundle, promote, rollback) is the same

docs.title: kardinal explain
docs.text: Explain the current state of a promotion pipeline

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
For each environment of (or just ), show the current Bundle's step and the gates it waits on, gates that are not ready first, with each gate's expression, state and reason, and what is deployed there now when the change has not landed yet. -w refreshes every 3 seconds.

Explain displays, per environment, the PromotionStep and the PolicyGates of the current Bundle there: the newest Bundle that is not Superseded and has a PromotionStep in that environment, or a gate instance there and has not failed. The Graph creates a Bundle's gate instances when the Bundle starts, so an environment a promoting Bundle has not reached yet shows the gates it will wait on; one a Failed Bundle never reached keeps the Bundle before it. When every Bundle there is Superseded, the newest one with a PromotionStep there is shown. Gates include org gates from the policy namespaces and skip-permission gates: they are the instances the Graph created for that Bundle, with the controller's latest evaluation. Gates that are not ready are listed first. VERSION names the version each row belongs to: its tag, then its Bundle ("1.5.0 (app-x7k2p)"). kardinal why says the same in a sentence per environment.

An environment where that Bundle's change has not landed yet (it has not reached the environment, or its PR is not merged) also gets a line after the table with the version deployed there now (its image tags or config commit, then its Bundle): the one whose change landed last, as kardinal rollback judges it. Image and config Bundles do not supersede each other: when the last one is an image Bundle and a config commit landed before it, the line adds "; config from ", and under a config Bundle it adds "; images from ". "deployed: none" means no change has landed there yet. 

prod   deployed: sha-1a2b3c4 (app-v1)
uat    deployed: sha-5d6e7f8 (app-v2); config 9f8e7d6 from app-cfg1

A gate's STATE is the one the UI shows, the first that applies:

Pass        ready
Block       holding the Bundle: every upstream environment is Verified
            and the environment has no step yet, or the gate holds
            the environment's Pending step
Superseded  the Bundle was superseded; the gate is not evaluated again
Rejected    the Bundle was rejected (kardinal reject); not evaluated again
Pending     not evaluated yet
Waiting     evaluated not ready, not holding the Bundle: the Bundle has
            not reached the environment, or it failed (it can retry)

kardinal explain <pipeline> [<env>] [flags]

docs.title: kardinal get pipelines
docs.text: List Pipelines

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
List Pipelines with the state of their current version in each environment, in DAG order (wide pipelines get one summary row each: kardinal get pipelines shows every environment). A failed build prints an ERROR: line with its cause after the table. -w refreshes it.

BUNDLE is the pipeline's current bundle: the newest bundle that is not Superseded, whatever its phase (the newest one when all are Superseded), the same bundle the UI shows. Every environment column describes that bundle: its step state there, in words ("Live", "Waiting for PR merge"); "Not reached" when it has no step there yet and is still promoting (held by a gate, or an upstream environment is not live yet). A dash means the bundle has no PromotionStep there and is finished (Verified, Failed or Superseded) or skips the environment or stops before it (skipEnvironments or targetEnvironment). kardinal status and kardinal explain instead pick the current bundle per environment, so for an environment the newest bundle has not reached they describe the bundle that was there before.

Environment columns follow the pipeline's DAG (waves and dependsOn), merged across the pipelines listed. With more than 8 environment columns (one wide pipeline, or several with different environments), each pipeline gets one summary row instead: ENVS, the environment count, and PROGRESS, the current bundle's states with counts, most advanced first ("42 Live, 108 Checking health"), and FURTHEST, the last environment in DAG order where the bundle is live (in a wave, the last one in spec order). kardinal get pipelines shows every environment of that pipeline.

-o json and -o yaml print the Pipeline objects as the API server lists them (by namespace, then name), without the table's columns, with the API's state values (Verified, WaitingForMerge).

The table needs list permission on bundles and promotionsteps; without it the command fails instead of showing dashes.

Use --watch / -w to stream live updates (polls every 2s, Ctrl-C to quit).

When a Bundle promotion fails (e.g. due to an invalid dependsOn reference or a circular dependency in the Pipeline spec), an ERROR: line is printed after the table with the pipeline name and root cause:

ERROR: pipeline my-app: build: environment "prod" dependsOn unknown environment "staging"

This avoids the need to run kubectl describe bundle to find the root cause of a stalled promotion.

docs.title: kardinal inbox
docs.text: List what waits for a person: on you first, then on others

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
List every environment that waits for a person, in the namespace (every namespace with -A): an approval, a gate that does not open by itself, a hold, a paused pipeline, a PR to merge. What you can move on comes first, with the command that does it; then what waits on someone else, and who.

inbox lists, per environment, what waits for a person, from each Pipeline's status.environments, the gate instances of the versions that wait, and its holds:

approval an approval gate that has not its quorum (n of m) and nobody rejected gate a gate that does not pass and does not open by itself (its expression reads nothing that changes with time; see ship) hold a hold (kardinal hold, rollback --hold) paused the pipeline is paused pr its PR waits for a person to merge it (not pr.merge.auto)

"Waiting on you" is what you can move on, with the command in NEXT: an approval your approval would count for, by the same tally the server keeps (allowedUsers, allowedGroups, excludeAuthor, one approval per person), when you may create Approvals; a gate, a hold or a pause when you hold the rights the API server and the chart's admission policies check (patch policygates and update policygates/override; update pipelines and pipelines/hold; patch pipelines and update pipelines/pause), asked with SelfSubjectAccessReviews. Everything else is "Waiting on someone else", with WHO: the allowed users and groups, someone other than you when you created the version, or the PR's reviewers. An approval excludeAuthor cannot enforce (no verified creator, or a kardinal component created the version) is on no one. A PR is never on you: the CLI cannot tell who may merge. Gates that open by themselves and promotions in flight are not listed. The oldest wait comes first.

A command carries -n when its namespace is not the kubeconfig context's. -A lists every namespace; when you may not list Pipelines cluster-wide it fails and says to use -n. A namespace whose gates or Bundles it may not read is noted on stderr. -o json|yaml prints {onYou, others, skipped}; each item has namespace, pipeline, environment, bundle, version, kind, waiting, onYou, who, next (without --reason : needsReason says it needs one) and since.

docs.title: kardinal init
docs.text: Write a Pipeline for your GitOps repository, from flags or a few questions

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Write the smallest Pipeline that promotes your environments, defaults left out: from flags (--repo makes it non-interactive), else the wizard asks for what the flags do not say. With a cluster it finds the Argo CD Applications or Flux Kustomizations to check health with; --create-secret makes the git Secret, --apply applies the Pipeline.

With --repo, init asks nothing: --name (default my-app), --envs (default test,uat,prod, in promotion order), --branch (default main), --strategy (kustomize, the default, or helm), --prod-approval (pr-review, the default, or auto: the last environment's approval) and --secret (default github-token) say the rest, and -n the namespace. Without --repo it asks for each of them that no flag gives, on a terminal or one answer per line from a pipe.

It writes the smallest Pipeline that says it, as examples/minimal does: a default (branch main, kustomize, approval auto, the default health check) is left out (also namespace default, unless -n gives it). The name, namespace and environments must be DNS-1123 labels, --repo an https or ssh git URL (https://host/owner/repo, ssh://git@host/owner/repo or git@host:owner/repo.git) with no spaces, query or fragment, and --branch a git branch name; every value is written as a YAML scalar and the YAML is decoded back and compared, so no value can add a field. When a cluster can be reached it looks, for each environment, for an Argo CD Application - in argocd or a Flux Kustomization - in flux-system, and sets health type argocd or flux where it finds one (--no-detect skips this). The Pipeline is checked as kardinal validate checks it before anything is written. Running init again with the same answers changes nothing ("unchanged") and succeeds; a file with another Pipeline is not overwritten without --force.

--create-secret creates the git Secret (key token) from $GITHUB_TOKEN, else from gh auth token, labelled kardinal.io/referenceable=true so the Pipeline may use it; an existing Secret is kept (and labelled). --apply creates the Pipeline; one of the same name and spec is unchanged, one with another spec is replaced only with --force.

Use --scaffold-gitops to also create the GitOps repository structure: environments//kustomization.yaml for each environment. The scaffold is Kustomize-only; it is skipped for the helm strategy.

Use --demo to scaffold with the kardinal-test-app placeholder image.

kardinal init [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
kardinal init --name my-app --repo https://github.com/myorg/gitops
  kardinal init --name my-app --repo https://github.com/myorg/gitops --envs dev,prod --create-secret --apply
  kardinal init
  kardinal init --demo --scaffold-gitops && kubectl apply -f pipeline.yaml

      --branch string          Base branch of the repository (default main)
      --create-secret          Create the git Secret from $GITHUB_TOKEN, else gh auth token, labelled for the Pipeline to use

docs.title: kardinal policy list
docs.text: List PolicyGates

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
List PolicyGate templates: every one, or those the controller attaches to 's environments. CEL is the controller's syntax check (valid, invalid, or - not checked yet); LAST-EVALUATED is the newest evaluation of the template's per-Bundle instances.

Without --pipeline, lists every template in every namespace. With --pipeline, lists the templates the controller attaches to that pipeline's environments.

The CEL column is the controller's syntax check of the expression: valid, invalid (see kubectl describe), or - when not checked yet.

The controller evaluates the per-Bundle instances the Graph creates from a template, never the template, so LAST-EVALUATED is the newest evaluation of the template's instances (with --pipeline, of that pipeline's instances), or - when none has been evaluated. docs.title: kardinal policy simulate
docs.text: Simulate PolicyGate evaluation for a hypothetical promotion context

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Evaluate the gates of as the controller would, for a Bundle that went through every upstream environment, at --time (UTC; default now) with --soak-minutes upstream. Nothing is written. The first line is RESULT: PASS or RESULT: BLOCKED, then each blocking gate with its message and the next hour it would pass; it exits 0 either way.

Selects the PolicyGates the controller attaches to the environment (the pipeline's namespace plus the policy namespaces, matched by the kardinal.io/applies-to label) and evaluates each one with the controller's PolicyGate reconciler, against a Bundle that has promoted through every upstream environment. Metrics, change windows and promotion history are read from the cluster; nothing is written to it. Metric results are used as they are now at every simulated time: a MetricCheck result is "Stale" only if it is stale now.

--time is UTC: a weekday and an hour ("Saturday 3pm", "tue 10:00", "15 Friday") or an RFC 3339 timestamp. The weekday is its next occurrence (today counts). Without --time the current time is used.

--soak-minutes is the soak time of every upstream environment (upstream..soakMinutes and bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes).

A blocked gate shows the next hour, within 7 days, at which it would pass with the same inputs. Gates that do not depend on time show no window.

The first line is RESULT: PASS or RESULT: BLOCKED. A blocked result then lists each blocking gate with its message and next window. Last comes one row per gate: its name, PASS or BLOCK, and the reason. The command exits 0 whether the result is PASS or BLOCKED, so a script reads the RESULT line; it exits non-zero only when it cannot simulate (a bad flag, a pipeline or environment that does not exist, or no cluster to read).

kardinal policy simulate <pipeline> <env> [flags]

kardinal policy simulate my-app prod --time "Saturday 3pm"
  # RESULT: BLOCKED
  # Blocked by: no-weekend-deploys

docs.text: Validate PolicyGate YAML syntax and dry-run CEL expressions

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Check every PolicyGate in a YAML file offline: each expression is compiled and evaluated as the controller would, now, for a Bundle with no images, metrics or history. PASS or FAIL per gate, UNKNOWN when it needs cluster data (use policy simulate). It exits non-zero only when an expression does not compile.

Each expression is compiled with the controller's PolicyGate CEL environment, then evaluated by the controller's reconciler against a local context: the current time, a Bundle with no images or provenance, no metrics, no upstream history and no change windows. The environment is the first entry of the gate's kardinal.io/applies-to label. The file is -f , as kardinal validate takes it, or the argument.

With no cluster there is no upstream environment: bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes is 0, as for a version that just reached the upstream, and when that decides the result (the gate would pass, or fail, once soaked) a Note says so (upstream..* has no entry, so such a gate is UNKNOWN). kardinal policy simulate --soak-minutes evaluates the gate with a soak.

Results: PASS the gate would allow promotion in that context FAIL the gate would block promotion in that context UNKNOWN the expression needs cluster data the local context lacks (metrics, upstream, bundle.pr); use 'kardinal policy simulate'

No cluster access is required. The command exits non-zero only when an expression does not compile.

docs.title: kardinal quickstart
docs.text: Install kardinal on a local cluster and promote a first version

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Set up a demo on a local cluster (kind, k3d, minikube, Docker or Rancher Desktop; any other context is refused before anything is written): kro, Argo CD, kardinal, the git Secret, the Argo CD Applications of your kardinal-demo fork, a Pipeline with an approval gate on prod, and a first version, which it follows until prod waits for your approval. A re-run changes nothing.

quickstart refuses, before it sends anything to a cluster, a kubeconfig context whose name is not kind-, k3d-, minikube, docker-desktop or rancher-desktop, or whose API server is not on this machine (loopback, 0.0.0.0, Docker Desktop's kubernetes.docker.internal; for minikube also its drivers' networks 192.168.49.0/24, 192.168.39.0/24 and 192.168.59.0/24). It also refuses to run while a variable is set that points helm, kubectl or client-go elsewhere (HELM_KUBE*, such as HELM_KUBECONTEXT, and KUBERNETES_MASTER), and refuses a context whose cluster has a proxy-url, or whose server an environment proxy (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY) applies to: the proxy decides where requests go. Go never proxies localhost and 127.0.0.1; for 0.0.0.0, host.docker.internal or a minikube address, add the host to NO_PROXY. There is no flag to override it, on purpose. Use --context to pick a local context. helm and kubectl run on a kubeconfig file with only that context, without KUBECONFIG or those variables, and kubectl with KUBERC=off. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops the step that runs and removes that file. What it cannot see: a loopback port that tunnels to a remote cluster (kubectl port-forward, ssh -L) looks local; do not point a local context at one.

On a local cluster it installs, each only when it is not there yet: kro (the version hack/install-kro.sh pins), with the Graph controller Argo CD (its release manifests, polling git every 10s instead of 2-3m; --no-argocd when the cluster has one, which keeps its own settings) kardinal-promoter (the chart of this CLI's version, in kardinal-system; --chart, --chart-version and --set for another) Then it applies, in default (so no command needs -n): the git Secret github-token, from $GITHUB_TOKEN, else gh auth token: the token needs contents and pull requests read and write on --repo an Argo CD ApplicationSet kardinal-test-app in argocd: the Applications kardinal-test-app- sync environments/ of --repo a PolicyGate prod-approval: prod waits for your approval (you, the user the cluster says you are; excludeAuthor is off) the Pipeline demo: test, uat and prod, all auto, prod behind the gate, health checked with the Applications It ships the first version (--image) unless demo has one, and follows it until prod waits for your approval (--no-wait does not follow). It does not change your kubeconfig. A re-run changes nothing.

Then: kardinal approve demo prod ships it to prod; kardinal dashboard opens the UI; the Next lines show the command that ships the next version. To get PR evidence for prod, set its approval to pr-review in the Pipeline.

kardinal quickstart --delete, behind the same local-context check, deletes the demo and nothing else: the demo's versions first (it waits up to 2m for the controller to close their open PRs, and stops there if they are not gone), then the Pipeline demo, the gate prod-approval and the ApplicationSet (Argo CD deletes its Applications), each only when quickstart applied it (field manager kardinal-quickstart), and the Secret github-token only when quickstart created it (label kardinal.io/quickstart) and no other Pipeline uses it. Without a Pipeline demo, only versions with that label go. Do not add the label by hand: --delete deletes what carries it. It keeps kro, Argo CD, kardinal-promoter with its token Secret, and the kardinal-test-app- namespaces, and prints the command that deletes those. It asks first on a terminal (--yes does not). A re-run deletes nothing. 

kardinal quickstart --repo <your fork of kardinal-demo> [flags]

  kardinal quickstart --repo https://github.com/<you>/kardinal-demo
  kardinal approve demo prod
  kardinal quickstart --delete

docs.title: kardinal reject
docs.text: Reject a version: it is never promoted again, and rollback never picks it

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Reject a version for good, with --reason, in your Kubernetes name. Steps that have not delivered it yet fail and their PRs close; steps whose change is live finish their health check. Rollback, promote and Subscriptions never pick it again. It does not revert an environment: use kardinal rollback for that.

Sets spec.rejected on the Bundle with your Kubernetes username (read from the API server with a SelfSubjectReview, as kubectl auth whoami does) and the reason. The Bundle turns Rejected, whatever its phase:

  • no new PromotionStep is created for it;
  • its steps that have not delivered the change (Pending, Promoting, or WaitingForMerge with the PR still open) fail, and their PRs are closed;
  • a step whose change is live (HealthChecking, or a PR that merged) keeps going and is health-checked;
  • kardinal rollback, onHealthFailure=rollback and kardinal promote never pick it or any Bundle carrying its images or config commit, and a Subscription creates no Bundle for them.

Rejecting is final: spec.rejected cannot be changed or removed. It does not revert an environment that already runs the Bundle; roll that environment back with kardinal rollback. See docs/reject.md.

kardinal reject <bundle|version> [flags]

  kardinal reject 1.5.0 --reason "CVE-2026-1234 in the base image"

docs.title: kardinal ship
docs.text: Ship a version: create a Bundle, and with --wait follow it

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Ship a version through : the same Bundle as kardinal create bundle, with the same flags. --wait follows it until it is live everywhere it goes (exit 0), fails (1), stops at a gate or a hold (3), waits for its PR to be merged (4), is replaced or rejected (5), or --timeout passes (6).

ship takes create bundle's flags and creates the same Bundle; create bundle stays. Without --wait it prints the Bundle's name and, on stderr, how to follow it.

--wait follows the Bundle, printing on stderr each new state of its environments after the time since the start (+1m5s), the URL of each PR it opens, and at the end a summary: each environment's last state and how long its own promotion there took ("took": from its first step's start, else from its upstream going live, else from the Bundle's creation), or how long it has waited in it ("for"). --quiet (-q) prints none of that. It ends with one line on stdout (or, with -o json, an object with bundle, pipeline, namespace, type, version, url, result, exitCode, message and the Bundle's environments from status.environments). Exit codes:

CODE RESULT WHEN 0 Verified live in every environment it promotes 1 Failed, Error it failed, or it could not be read three times in a row (or the command itself failed) 3 Held a person is needed and nothing else of it is moving: an approval gate, a hold, a paused pipeline, or a gate that does not pass and does not open by itself (with --stop-at-gate, any gate that does not pass) 4 WaitingForMerge its PR waits for a person to merge it (not one the SCM merges by itself, pr.merge.auto), and nothing else of it is moving 5 Superseded, Rejected, Deleted a newer version replaced it, it was rejected, or it was deleted 6 Timeout, Interrupted --timeout (default 30m) passed, or Ctrl-C or SIGTERM interrupted the wait; the result is printed first

A stop at a gate, a hold or a PR counts once two reads agree, and a gate not evaluated yet never stops it. A gate that does not pass is waited for, until --timeout, when it opens by itself: its expression, outside its string literals, reads one of these variables that change with time (with a . or [ after it: schedule.hour, schedule["hour"]):

schedule schedule.isWeekend, schedule.hour, schedule.dayOfWeek upstream upstream..soakMinutes and every other field of upstream. bundle.upstreamSoakMinutes the soak of the environment before this one metrics metrics..value, metrics..result changewindow changewindow.

So CI can wait through a soak or a schedule. A PR the SCM merges by itself (pr.merge.auto) is waited for too. Any other gate that does not pass (on a Bundle label, its provenance, its version) needs a person: exit 3, as do an approval gate, a hold and a paused pipeline. --stop-at-gate stops at any gate that does not pass. Stopping to follow does not stop the promotion: kardinal status -w goes on following it. The codes are stable: a new outcome gets a new code. 

kardinal ship <pipeline> --image <ref> [flags]

  kardinal ship my-app --image ghcr.io/org/my-app:1.5.0 --wait --timeout 1h

  # in CI: the Bundle's name and the outcome as JSON
  kardinal ship my-app --image "$IMAGE" --wait -o json | jq -r .result

With one: per environment, the version running there, a newer one on its way in, its state and since when, its PR, and the gates holding it back. Run it first when a promotion is stuck; -w refreshes it and -o json prints it for scripts.

When called without arguments, across every namespace (-n for one). When you may not list every namespace it shows the kubeconfig's, with a note on stderr; with -A, which asks for every namespace, it fails and says to use -n:

Controller: v0.10.1 in kardinal-system, 1/1 ready Pipelines: 3 (1 degraded: team-b/api) Versions: 5 (3 in flight)

NAMESPACE PIPELINE SUMMARY team-a web 1.5.0 live in test, prod team-b api A version failed team-c edge 7.2.0 live in canary and 27 of 42 pops; promoting in 5 pops; queued in 10 pops

Details: kardinal status -n

the controller version (the kardinal-version ConfigMap in --controller-namespace) and how many replicas of its Deployment are ready (else "no controller Deployment found there: kardinal doctor", or "can't read the controller Deployment (needs list on deployments in )": the chart's user roles do not grant it; fewer ready than desired is a warning), the pipeline count with any Degraded pipelines, the version count (in flight = Available or Promoting), and one line per pipeline (at most 50; then kardinal get pipelines -A) with its status.summary sentence (its phase from a controller that predates it). -o json adds controllerReady, controllerHealth {ready, reason}, namespace and note (when it is not every namespace) and items [{namespace, pipeline, phase, summary}] to controller, pipelines, degraded, bundles and activeBundles.

When called with a pipeline name: first the Pipeline's own problems, an ERROR when it is not Ready (such as GitCredentialMissing, with the command that creates the git Secret, or SecretNotReferenceable, with the command that labels it kardinal.io/referenceable=true); then the Pipeline's summary sentence ("1.5.0 live in test; waiting for PR merge in prod (#42)"), then one row per environment (a fleet environment expands to its targets) from the Pipeline's status.environments, which the controller writes:

RUNNING the Bundle whose change runs there, with its version INCOMING a newer Bundle on its way in, with its version STATE where the newest Bundle there stands, in words ("Live", "Waiting for PR merge", "Held by gate no-weekend-deploys", "Held by rollback") SINCE how long it has been in that state PR the pull request it waits for, while it waits for its merge

REGION, after ENVIRONMENT, shows where each environment runs when one of them health-checks another cluster: the health.kubeconfigSecretRef Secret. -o wide adds ACTIVE STEP, the step the newest Bundle there is on (git-clone, open-pr, health-check, ...).

Then the gates holding a version back, with their CEL expression cut to 40 characters, their message and when each was last checked; and a WARNING: line for a Rejected Bundle whose change still runs somewhere, with the rollback that removes it. A pipeline nothing was shipped to yet says so, with the command that ships the first version.

With a controller older than status.environments, the CLI computes the same rows itself, with the controller's code; SINCE is then known only for live environments. -o json and -o yaml print the same data with the API's state values (Verified, WaitingForMerge) and "source": "controller" or "cli". kardinal explain shows the steps and every gate of the current Bundle.

kardinal status [<pipeline>] [flags]

docs.title: kardinal validate
docs.text: Validate Pipeline and PolicyGate YAML before applying to the cluster

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Check Pipeline and PolicyGate YAML offline: environments, the dependency graph, fields the controller does not implement, and every gate expression compiles. It exits 1 with the errors when the file is not valid; kubectl apply --dry-run=server checks the full schema.

Validate Pipeline and PolicyGate YAML without connecting to the cluster. The file may hold several documents; each kardinal.io Pipeline and PolicyGate is checked. Other objects (a Namespace, another API group's Pipeline) are skipped with a note.

Checks: - Every document: no field the CRD does not define (kubectl apply's strict field validation refuses it), named with its path. - Pipeline: at least one environment, every environment named, spec.git.url set, the environment dependencies form a valid graph (no cycles, no unknown dependsOn), and no reserved field that is not implemented is set (autoRollback, a health.resource.kind other than Deployment). The controller reports the same fields as Ready=False/NotImplemented on the Pipeline. With metadata.namespace set, a git.secretRef in another namespace is an error too (the controller reports it as Ready=False/ValidationFailed). With --allowed-repositories (the controller's scm.allowedRepositories), a Pipeline must point spec.git.url at one of them unless it never needs the controller's SCM token: a git.secretRef and no pr-review environment (the controller reports Ready=False/RepositoryNotAllowed); with --scm-provider bitbucket-datacenter a URL is matched as KEY/slug, as the controller does. - PolicyGate: spec.expression set and compiles with the controller's PolicyGate CEL environment, and a name of at most 63 characters (the API server rejects a longer one); spec.when is a warning (it is ignored)

This is not full CRD schema validation; 'kubectl apply --dry-run=server' checks the schema.

Exit codes: 0: file is valid 1: validation failed (actionable errors printed)

kardinal validate [flags]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
kardinal validate -f pipeline.yaml
  kardinal validate -f examples/ --allowed-repositories github.com/acme/*

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
--allowed-repositories strings   The controller's scm.allowedRepositories (comma-separated host/repository globs): report a Pipeline that would need the controller's SCM token for a spec.git.url that is not one of them
  -f, --file string                    Path to Pipeline or PolicyGate YAML file (required)
  -h, --help                           help for validate
      --scm-provider string            The controller's scm.provider, for --allowed-repositories: with bitbucket-datacenter a spec.git.url is matched as KEY/slug however it names the repository (/scm/, browse or ssh path), as the controller does

docs.title: kardinal why
docs.text: Say why an environment waits, and what moves it on

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
Say, for of (or each environment), in a sentence what it waits for, then the version, the gate or PR, and the command that moves it on. -o wide prints kardinal explain's table instead; -o json and yaml print explain's entries. -w refreshes every 3 seconds.

why answers, per environment, in one sentence what it waits for, then the details and the command that moves it on:

prod is waiting for your approval. Version 1.5.0 (my-app-x7k2p) Gate cab · 0 of 1 approvals Next kardinal approve my-app prod

The cases, in the order it checks them: the pipeline is paused (Next: kardinal resume); the environment is held (on what, by whom, why; Next: kardinal unhold); a gate holds it (an approval: how many of how many, and "your approval" only when your approval would count: you are in allowedUsers or allowedGroups, or both are empty, with excludeAuthor you did not create the version, and yours is not counted yet ("approval by someone else (you approved)" once it is); else who may, "approval by alice or group release-managers"; who rejected it, when someone did; nobody, when the policy cannot be met. These come from the server's own tally of the gate's Approvals, so why and the controller agree; any other gate: its message, Rule its expression, Now its last evaluation (for a soak gate, how far the version soaked: "soak 0.4 of 3 min in uat"), Opens when it opens and how often it is rechecked ("by itself in about 2m36s" for a soak gate); Next: kardinal approve; for a gate that opens by itself, wait, with kardinal override only as Or; else kardinal override); its PR waits to be merged (PR and its URL); the version failed (Why the step's message; Next: kardinal logs, or roll back); it is promoting; it waits for an upstream environment; it has no version yet; or nothing is waiting ("prod runs 1.5.0 and nothing is waiting.").

why shows the gates the version started with. A version gets its gates when it starts promoting, so a gate created or edited later applies to the versions shipped after it, not to one already waiting (Policy Gates, "When a new or edited gate takes effect").

-o wide prints kardinal explain's table (every step and gate of the current version, with kinds and expressions), with the commands that get past a gate on stderr; -o json and yaml print explain's entries.

kardinal why <pipeline> [<env>] [flags]

  kardinal why my-app prod -o wide

docs.title: kardinal
docs.text: kardinal manages promotion pipelines on Kubernetes

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
kardinal promotes versions of your application through environments, with gates, pull requests and health checks, on Kubernetes.

Getting started: kardinal quickstart --repo try it on a local cluster kardinal init --name my-app --repo write a Pipeline for your repository kardinal ship my-app --image app:1.4 --wait ship a version and follow it kardinal why my-app prod why it waits, and what moves it on

Output follows where it goes. On a terminal, each state reads as a glyph and its label in the status colours of the UI, from its design tokens (web/tokens/tokens.json): Live (spruce), Promoting and Checking health (thread red), Waiting for PR merge and gates not ready yet (dusk blue), Held by gate (ochre), Failed (on garnet, the only filled state), Replaced by newer version and Not reached (grey); Paused and Held by rollback are bold. Without COLORTERM=truecolor and a COLORFGBG that names the background, they are the nearest of the 16 ANSI colours, which the terminal's theme adapts. Without a UTF-8 locale the glyphs are ASCII (* Live, ~ Waiting for PR merge).

Piped to a file or another program, or with NO_COLOR (any value) or TERM=dumb, output is plain words: the labels without glyphs or colour. The cluster's text (a step's message, a Pipeline's summary) passes through as it is when the locale is UTF-8 (LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE or LANG); without a UTF-8 locale, or with TERM=dumb, everything is ASCII (a dash is "-", an arrow "->", any other non-ASCII character "?"). On Windows, colour needs a console with virtual-terminal processing; without it output has no colour.

-o json and -o yaml print the API's values (Verified, WaitingForMerge) and the cluster's text unchanged, and no table placeholders ("-", "--", "..."): a field with nothing to say is left out. With -w, -o json prints one document per refresh and -o yaml separates them with "---". Hints, prompts and the CLI's own warnings go to stderr, so stdout stays valid JSON. The notices a report shows about what it read (the ERROR: and WARNING: lines of status, get pipelines and explain) are part of its output, on stdout, so kardinal status my-app | less shows them; with -o json they are fields. get prints the objects as the API server lists them. The others print these fields (in brackets the ones left out when empty):

create bundle, promote, rollback: bundle, pipeline, namespace, url, [type, version]; promote adds environment and from (the Bundle copied); rollback adds environment, rollbackOf (the Bundle restored), [replaces] (the one replaced) and, with --hold, hold {environment, bundle, [reason, expiresAt]} create bundle --dry-run: pipeline, namespace, nodes, environments [{name, [gates]}] in promotion order, [type, version, compact] unhold (release-hold): pipeline, namespace, environment, bundle (the version it was held on), url, [createdBy, reason] status: controller, pipelines, bundles, activeBundles, [degraded] (namespace/name) status : pipeline, namespace, source ("controller" or "cli"), environments, blockingGates, [phase, paused, summary, notices, warnings, regions]; an environment is status.environments' entry: name, [bundle, version, incomingBundle, incomingVersion, state, since, blockedBy, prURL, held]; a gate: name, instance, environment, bundle, expression, [message, reason, lastEvaluatedAt] explain: pipeline, namespace, entries [{environment, bundle, type (Step or PolicyGate), name, state, [expression, reason]}], [holds [{environment, bundle, [createdBy, reason, bundleMissing]}]] history: a list of {bundle, action (promote or rollback), environment, state, createdAt, [prURL, durationSeconds, running]}: durationSeconds once the step ended, running while it runs ship: the create bundle fields and exitCode, with --wait also [result, message, environments]

url is the pipeline in the UI: KARDINAL_UI_URL, else the address kardinal dashboard opens (http://localhost:8082/ui/). For example kardinal create bundle my-app --image app:1.4 -o json | jq -r .bundle names the new Bundle.
